item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La estatal chilena Codelco, una de las mayores productoras mundiales de cobre, anunció el lunes que firmó un acuerdo con la minera global BHP para la exploración de su pertenencia minera Anillo, ubicada en la región de Antofagasta en el norte de Chile. BHP podrá invertir hasta 40 millones de dólares para explorar y estudiar el potencial minero de las pertenencias. La firma del contrato se concretó la semana pasada durante la London Metal Exchange Week 2026, dijo un comunicado de la estatal, luego de completarse las autorizaciones legales para la constitución de derechos sobre pertenencias mineras de Codelco que no forman parte de yacimientos en actual explotación. El acuerdo para exploración se había anunciado el año pasado.

item.title: From Amazon to Google, the deep-pocketed investors in Anthropic
item.description: Only a few startups have attracted as much investor conviction as Anthropic. Backed by some of the biggest names in technology and finance, the AI company has seen its valuation soar through successive funding rounds.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Only a few startups have attracted as much investor conviction as Anthropic. Backed by some of the biggest names in technology and finance, the AI company has seen its valuation soar through successive funding rounds. Its [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"initial public offering"] now offers a closely watched test of whether investors beyond Silicon Valley share that enthusiasm for the leaders of the AI boom. Here's a look at the key investors backing the Claude maker: Investor Details Amazon Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and in April agreed to invest up to an additional $20 billion. Anthropic also committed to spend more than $100 billion on the e-commerce giant's cloud services over 10 years Alphabet's Google Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic, including an initial $10 billion investment announced in April. The partnership provides Anthropic with cloud infrastructure and access to Google's AI chips, which are used to train and run Claude models Spark Capital Spark Capital led Anthropic's $450 million Series C round in May 2023 and gained board representation through general partner Yasmin Razavi Lightspeed Venture Partners Lightspeed led the $3.5 billion Series E round in March 2025 and later co-led the $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation in September that year Fidelity Management & Research Fidelity participated in Series E and co-led the $13 billion Series F financing at a $183 billion valuation. The firm's other investments include Databricks and CoreWeave Salesforce Ventures Salesforce Ventures participated in the $450 million Series C round and the $3.5 billion Series E financing. The software firm's venture arm has also invested in firms such as Cohere and Chainguard ICONIQ Capital ICONIQ led the $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation and later co-led the $30 billion Series G financing. The venture capital firm's investments include OpenAI and smart ring maker Oura GIC Singapore's sovereign wealth fund led the $30 billion Series G round at a $380 billion valuation. GIC has also invested in AI voice generation startup ElevenLabs Coatue Management Coatue led the $30 billion Series G financing and later co-led the $65 billion Series H round. The investment firm has also financed companies such as Canva and CoreWeave D1 Capital Partners D1 Capital invested across multiple large financings including Series E, Series F, Series G and Series H. The firm has holdings in Cognition AI and SpaceX Sequoia Capital Sequoia was a significant investor in Series G and became one of the lead investors in the $65 billion Series H round at a $965 billion valuation Altimeter Capital Altimeter invested in the September 2025 $13 billion fundraise and was a lead investor in the $65 billion Series H financing at a $965 billion valuation Jaan Tallinn Skype co-founder Tallinn led Anthropic's first institutional financing, a $124 million Series A round in 2021. The angel investor has also funded open-source AI startup Zyphra and Rain AI Eric Schmidt The former Google chief executive has backed Anthropic personally and is among the company's best-known individual investors. Schmidt has also funded Yann LeCun's Advanced Machine Intelligence Menlo Ventures Menlo participated in major late-stage financings, including the $3.5 billion Series E round at a $61.5 billion valuation

item.title: Egypt approves military support for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks escalate
item.description: The move could push Cairo directly into the regional conflict that has expanded with intensified attacks by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on the Gulf kingdom.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Parliament authorised Egypt's military on Monday to provide support to help defend Saudi Arabia, parliamentarians said and local media reported, a move that could push Cairo directly into the regional conflict that has expanded with intensified attacks by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on the Gulf kingdom. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi had [USN:L6N46403J TEXT:"asked parliament"] last week to approve defending its Gulf Arab ally and the world's biggest oil exporter if Riyadh requests help against the Houthis, whose advances also threaten the strategic [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] — a gateway to Egypt's Suez Canal. Egypt has frequently condemned Iranian and Iranian-backed attacks on Gulf countries but has not publicly engaged in direct combat or joined the Mecca [USN:L1N45R0S7 TEXT:"mutual defence"] pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey that was [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"signed in August"]. Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said this month that Egyptian membership in the pact remains "under serious consideration." Egypt, the Arab world's most populous state with one of the region's largest militaries, joined the Saudi-led coalition in an earlier phase of Yemen's war in March 2015 mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes while pledging air support. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but played only a limited combat role. Egypt was involved in a costly military intervention in Yemen in the 1960s and has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War. Saudi Arabia is a major political and financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, deposits at the central bank and energy supplies under Sisi. Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthi militia, which controls the capital Sanaa, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming a volatile front in the US-Israeli war on Iran . The Houthis have attacked [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"Riyadh's international airport"] and the state oil giant [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Aramco"], disrupting flights and oil exports, while aid agencies have warned of worsening conditions in Yemen, already suffering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. Abdelatty and Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders rather than attacking Yemen. Abdelatty said after that visit that Cairo advocates exploring [USN:L1N4680Z9 TEXT:""every opportunity""] to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically. The Saudi crown prince [USN:S8N452004 TEXT:"visited Sisi in Cairo"] on September 15 to discuss security and navigation in the Red Sea after the fighting in Yemen reignited.

item.title: Taxas dos DIs de longo prazo sobem mais de 260 pontos-base após vitória de Lula
item.description: As taxas dos DIs dispararam nesta manhã de segunda-feira após o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vencer o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, surpreendendo o mercado.
item.dc:creator: Fabricio Castro
item.content:encoded: As taxas dos DIs dispararam nesta manhã de segunda-feira após o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vencer o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, surpreendendo o mercado. Às 9h58, a taxa do DI (Depósito Interfinanceiro) para janeiro de 2028 estava em 14,915%, em alta de 206 pontos-base ante o ajuste de 12,859% da sessão anterior. Na ponta longa da curva a termo, a taxa do DI para janeiro de 2035 estava em 15,375%, com elevação de 263 pontos-base ante 12,745%. Lula venceu a disputa pelo Planalto com 51,79% dos votos válidos, contra 48,21% do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Como o mercado estava em grande parte posicionado para uma vitória de Flávio, o ajuste nesta manhã é intenso. Na noite de domingo, profissionais consultados pela Reuters já haviam [USN:L2N46C034 TEXT:"projetado"] um forte avanço das taxas dos DIs, em especial nos contratos com prazos mais longos, que refletem mais diretamente a perspectiva para a política fiscal. No dia seguinte ao primeiro turno, quando Flávio ficou à frente de Lula, a taxa do DI para janeiro de 2035 chegou a ceder mais de 130 pontos-base, em meio à euforia do mercado com a possibilidade de o senador vencer a disputa. Por trás da euforia estava a leitura de que, com Flávio no Planalto, cresceriam as chances de um ajuste nas contas públicas. Como Lula venceu o segundo turno, garantindo mais um mandato, a curva a termo brasileira está enfrentando um forte ajuste de alta nesta segunda-feira. Em função das oscilações, a B3 elevou, por meio de comunicado, todos os limites de alta das taxas dos DIs, em todos os vencimentos. Em outra medida, o Tesouro Nacional informou nesta manhã o [USN:S0N45S019 TEXT:"cancelamento"] do tradicional leilão de títulos indexados à inflação na terça-feira e o cancelamento do leilão de papéis prefixados na quinta-feira. Por outro lado, o Tesouro manteve o leilão de Letras Financeiras do Tesouro (LFTs), títulos indexados à taxa básica Selic, previsto para terça-feira. Ao anunciar os cancelamentos, o Tesouro busca não estimular taxas ainda mais elevadas nos mercados de títulos e de DIs. item.title: Surgery Partners to be taken private by Bon Secours affiliate in $5.7 billion deal
item.description: Surgery Partners said on Monday it would be taken private by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt, sending its shares up 46%.
item.dc:creator: Christy Santhosh
item.content:encoded: Surgery Partners (SGRY.O) said on Monday it would be taken private by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt, sending its shares up 46%. Private equity group Bain Capital, which has been a minority shareholder since 2017 and owns 39% of Surgery Partners, will back the deal and retain a major ownership stake after closing, the companies said. The remaining shareholders will receive $23.50 per share, implying a premium of 49% to the stock's last close. The deal, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, highlights a growing push into outpatient surgery by healthcare operators, with not-for-profit health system Ascension having purchased surgical firm AmSurg for $3.9 billion earlier this year. The addition of Surgery Partners will expand Bon Secours Mercy Health's US footprint well beyond its more than 45 hospitals, according to the hospital system, adding over 200 sites across 30 states and about 5,000 affiliated physicians. The deal also ends a two-year strategic review during which Surgery Partners drew interest from potential buyers including Bain Capital, [USN:L4N3SK0YE TEXT:"whose bid to"] take the company private last year was rebuffed. Surgery Partners operates outpatient surgery centers, short-stay hospitals and related healthcare services across the US. "From a strategic perspective, there is some market overlap in Ohio and Kentucky, but the potential transaction would substantially broaden the system's (Bon Secours Mercy Health) national footprint, so we do not expect meaningful FTC antitrust risk issues," said Mizuho analyst Ann Hynes. Hynes said Bain retaining its ownership position under the proposed transaction is expected to help the deal close. In 2025, Surgery Partners generated $3.31 billion in revenue and reported an adjusted profit of 47 cents per share.

item.title: Netanyahu touts Trump endorsement on eve of vote, suggests they may restart war on Iran
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job".
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer, Emily Rose
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job". "US President Donald Trump has come with a friendship that has never existed before between an Israeli prime minister and an American president. And it is doubtful we will ever have such a friendly president again," Netanyahu said in a televised appearance late on Sunday night. "He has another two years, and he says he is calling on you to vote for me." In his own social media post on Sunday, Trump, who launched the Iran war jointly with Netanyahu in February, said: "Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started!" Netanyahu said Trump was willing to take action "that would finally, finally, remove the Iranian threat", but only as long as Netanyahu himself remains in power. "And I have already instructed the Mossad and the IDF (military) to bring down this regime, to bring down this regime because that is the only way to put an end to this threat," Netanyahu said, referring to Israel's main intelligence service and military. Asked for comment on Netanyahu's remarks, White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly said: “As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait." "The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]," Kelly added via email, referring to the November 3 vote in the US. Netanyahu's leading opponent, centrist former military Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, posted his own comments on social media, praising Trump as "a true friend of Israel". "I value his efforts and his commitment to Israel’s security, and I am confident that he will work in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people." EISENKOT ACCUSES NETANYAHU OF FEAR-MONGERING Tuesday's vote, Israel's first since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, is the first chance for voters to deliver a [USN:L8N4680E4 TEXT:"verdict on the worst security failure"] in generations and the wars on multiple fronts that followed. With Netanyahu already at the helm of the most right-wing government in Israeli history, politics have shifted even further to the right. Nearly all Jewish-led parties, including that of the hawkish Eisenkot, now [USN:L6N4660BW TEXT:"oppose the "two-state solution" that underpinned decades of peace negotiations"] with the Palestinians. But many voters say the divisive politics of Israel's longest-serving leader make the country weaker. Polls suggest Netanyahu's Likud Party will lose seats, potentially depriving his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties of its narrow majority. Eisenkot and an array of opposition parties ranging from the rump of the centre-left to the right, also have no clear path to unseat him. Netanyahu, 77, is an unrivaled master of political survival: the only time since 2009 that opponents managed to wrest him briefly from the premiership, it took four inconclusive elections within two years to get him out. He was back 18 months later. Neither side planned major public events for Monday. But both posted on social media, drumming on the election's major themes — for Netanyahu, that he is the only leader with the mettle to face down Israel's enemies; for his opponents, that his divisive politics have weakened the country. Netanyahu shared an AI-generated video on Monday of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, whose father Ali Khamenei was killed on the first night of US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Lying in a hospital bed, the younger Khamenei says his own vote would be "definitely not Bibi. Another term like this and I will be meeting my father sooner than expected." On Sunday Netanyahu posted a computer-generated photo of a mushroom cloud over Tel Aviv, saying Israel was in existential danger from Iran. [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Eisenkot responded"] by accusing him of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies, and threats—including images of nuclear bombs in the heart of Tel Aviv. This time, it won’t work for him." Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu carries its own political risks a week before a legislative election in which his own Republicans are seeking to hold onto power. The Iran war is deeply unpopular in the United States, blamed for a surge in prices especially for fuel. Major fighting has been suspended for months after ceasefire negotiations held without Israeli participation.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows explosive growth, risks and staggering costs
item.description: Anthropic disclosed steep losses and red-hot revenue growth in its US IPO filing on Monday, as the Claude-parent laid out its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology.
item.dc:creator: Manya Saini, Echo Wang
item.content:encoded: Anthropic disclosed steep losses and red-hot revenue growth in its US IPO filing on Monday, as the Claude-parent laid out its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology. The prospectus highlights [USN:L4N4691FD TEXT:"the AI company's rapid growth"] over the past year, fueled by Big Tech's breakneck spending that has driven a rally in AI stocks while raising concerns about lofty valuations and rising debt. The company also flagged growing risks from AI technology, underscoring concerns over its potential to cause harm which had led CEO Dario Amodei to call for a slowdown in development of advanced models. Anthropic's net loss in the first half of 2026 [USN:L4N4661JI TEXT:"widened sharply"] to $80.7 billion, largely due to a rise in the fair value of bonds convertible into company's shares. Revenue in this period stood at about $16.3 billion. The company's revenue grew a staggering 1,368% in the three months ended June 30 from a year ago, but warned in the prospectus that revenue growth rate could decline over time and fluctuate from time to time. The IPO, which is likely to be as early as later this month, is expected to establish Anthropic, the AI lab behind the viral Claude models, as a benchmark for how Wall Street values leading AI companies, including rival OpenAI. [USN:L6N46811V TEXT:"The IPO push comes"] despite a once-busy fall listing calendar thinning out as choppy markets prompt companies to delay their offerings. Analysts [USN:L6N46C0UF TEXT:"said"] that would give Anthropic access to a deep pool of capital to fund its costly AI ambitions. [USN:L6N4611C1 TEXT:"Growing investor uneasy"] with the debt-fueled AI investment boom has led to a global selloff in AI and tech stocks as they start to doubt if the trillions spent on data centers, chips and computing capacity will generate fast returns to support lofty valuations. Higher borrowing costs and rising bond yields have added to their caution. However, tech companies are still hungry for cash. Meta [USN:L3N46C0RT TEXT:"is aiming"] to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, while SpaceX has [USN:L6N46C0RJ TEXT:"inked"] a $40 billion deal with Apollo to lease AI chips and server hardware. VALUATION EXPECTATIONS Some current and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611F6 TEXT:"are valuing Anthropic"] at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a week ago, after the AI startup disclosed some financial details at a [USN:L6N4601DE TEXT:"recent investor event"], Reuters reported. "While Anthropic is well-capitalized, an IPO would give the company some valuable financial flexibility. No company wants to spend too long on the cusp of going public, since that can be a distraction," said Matt Kennedy, senior strategist at Renaissance Capital, a provider of IPO-focused research and ETFs "Maybe they could have gotten a higher valuation next year, but they've decided to "rip the band-aid off". The filing [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"confirmed a series of Reuters "][USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"exclusives"] that offered an early peek at its contents before Anthropic made it public, including details of its financial performance, growth trajectory and IPO plans. BALANCING AI'S PROMISES AND PERILS Anthropic said more than half of Fortune 500 companies and over 30% of Global 2000 firms were customers generating at least $100,000 each in revenue for the company over the 12 months ended September 30. The IPO comes as Anthropic's own research raises concerns about advanced AI systems, which in controlled tests have shown behaviors including code sabotage, fraud assistance and information manipulation. The findings have fueled concerns about how companies can keep powerful AI systems under control as they race to deploy them commercially. The prospectus also [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"highlighted risks"] associated with its AI models, which it said could exhibit "self-preserving behaviors", including behavior "resembling blackmail". "Our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures," it said. The company said it relies on a limited number of cloud services providers such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft and suppliers such as Broadcom for compute and critical parts of its infrastructure These relationships can create "dependencies and potential vulnerabilities", it said. Anthropic will trade on the Nasdaq after the [USN:L4N469189 TEXT:"IPO closes"] under the ticker symbol "ANT". The filing [USN:L4N41X0QE TEXT:"did not reveal"] the terms of its offering, including the number of shares it plans to sell and the proposed price range. RED HOT GROWTH Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers, was [USN:L4N4251UW TEXT:"valued at $965 billion"] in May in a funding round that drew some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley and Wall Street. Amazon and Google were among Anthropic's early strategic partners, investing billions of dollars in the startup while providing the cloud infrastructure needed to train and deploy Claude models. "We believe this abundance of AI will rapidly transform every sector of the global economy in ways greater than the impact of industrialization, electricity, semiconductors and the internet," the prospectus said. The company said it expects compute and infrastructure expenses to increase in absolute dollars and remain its largest operating expense for the foreseeable future. Anthropic remains locked in a fierce battle with OpenAI to lead the race to build the most advanced AI systems. The ChatGPT maker confidentially filed for an IPO in June and is expected to list by early 2027. Anthropic's IPO follows that of Elon Musk's SpaceX, which rewrote the IPO record books in June, when it [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"priced"] a $75 billion offering that valued the company at $1.75 trillion. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley were named as the lead banks for the IPO alongside 20 others as underwriters. Morgan Stanley will act as a stabilization agent, overseeing the stock's early trading. The roles mark another major win for Goldman and Morgan Stanley as they had led SpaceX's IPO too.

item.title: Ukraine has waited nearly a month for US to sign off on Patriot missiles, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Ukraine has been waiting for almost a month for the US defence secretary to sign off on critical missile supplies, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine has been waiting for almost a month for the US defence secretary to sign off on critical missile supplies, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure. "In particular, we have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS. I instructed our team to raise this with the American side once again," Zelenskiy said on X. The Ukrainian leader has repeatedly called on the US, which supplies missiles purchased by NATO allies under a program known as PURL, to speed up deliveries ahead of winter. Last week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged that a batch of interceptors may not have been delivered, but said that the delay was not for political reasons. Delayed missile deliveries are adding to Ukraine's tensions with the US after President Donald Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia and criticised Zelenskiy for Ukraine's unwillingness to stop attacks on Russian refineries. In recent weeks, Ukraine said that at some point it experienced gaps in getting intelligence from the US on Russian missile attacks. It also reported that [USN:L2N46A00O TEXT:"Starlink's military version"] has been throttled for days, disrupting military operations and air defences. Reuters has reported that the [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"order to throttle"] Starshield came from inside the White House. Both SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and US officials have said publicly that any decisions on Starlink and Starshield limitations could only have been taken by the other.

item.title: T-Mobile debuts wireless plans with customizable perks from streaming to food delivery
item.description: T-Mobile on Monday unveiled wireless plans that let customers pick and swap perks from Netflix to DoorDash, moving away from its traditional strategy of locking benefits into fixed plan tiers.
item.dc:creator: Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: T-Mobile (TMUS.O) on Monday unveiled wireless plans that let customers pick and swap perks from Netflix to DoorDash, moving away from its traditional strategy of locking benefits into fixed plan tiers. The move mirrors customizable offerings from rivals such as Verizon, but T-Mobile's new plans include selected streaming, music and other subscriptions at no extra cost beyond the monthly plan price. T-Mobile is betting that offering greater control over benefits will attract customers spending on multiple subscriptions, as competition among US carriers moves beyond network coverage and smartphone promotions Netflix was the most popular benefit in a pilot launched in early October, T-Mobile Chief Marketing Officer Allan Samson told Reuters in an interview Music subscriptions and artificial intelligence services also drew interest, while Xbox gaming was popular among younger customers, he added The new T-Mix plans will be available from next month in three tiers. The Standard tier is priced from $55 for one line, while More starts at $75 and Loaded at $95 The number of perks available will depend on the tier and the number of lines required Partnerships include Apple, DoorDash, Google, Hulu, Netflix, Paramount+, SiriusXM, Xbox and YouTube Customers can also select benefits including Delta SkyMiles, ESPN Unlimited, Google Gemini and device promotions Customers will be able to change selected perks every three months, or during an annual change window. Certain wireless benefits, such as satellite connectivity, can be changed at any time

item.title: Apollo deepens Abu Dhabi ties with investment in Mubadala Capital
item.description: Apollo Global Management will acquire a minority stake in Mubadala Capital and commit capital across its investment strategies, the alternative asset management subsidiary of Abu Dhabi wealth fund Mubadala said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will acquire a minority stake in Mubadala Capital and commit capital across its investment strategies, the alternative asset management subsidiary of Abu Dhabi wealth fund Mubadala said on Monday. The US investment group is expected to commit an aggregate $5 billion to Mubadala Capital’s investment strategies together with other strategic investors, which will join as minority shareholders, Mubadala Capital said in a statement. The deal deepens its ties with Mubadala. Apollo will acquire a stake of nearly 10% in the subsidiary, a person familiar with the matter said. Apollo declined to comment on the size of the stake. "Apollo’s investment will help the firm broaden its investor base, expand its strategies, and pursue new opportunities globally," Mubadala Capital said. It added that it will continue to operate independently and will maintain its own governance structure once the deal is completed. In recent years, global investment companies have boosted their presence and ties with the Gulf region, attracted by proximity to some of the world's largest sovereign wealth funds. Wealth funds in Abu Dhabi alone together manage an estimated $1.8 trillion. Mubadala, which had assets under management of $385 billion at the end of last year, is among funds that have been increasing exposure to alternative investments. Last year, Mubadala Capital entered into a $1 billion strategic partnership with New York-based investment firm Fortress to invest in private credit, following previous partnerships with Goldman Sachs and Apollo. "Mubadala has been a trusted partner in seeding and scaling a number of our strategies over the years. This investment in the differentiated asset management platform they have built in Mubadala Capital builds on our existing partnership and reflects our conviction in their business," John Zito, co-president of Apollo Asset Management, said in the statement. Goldman Sachs and Jefferies advised Mubadala Capital, while Morgan Stanley acted as financial advisor to Apollo for the deal, which is expected to close in the fourth quarter.

item.title: Oleshky: the occupied Ukrainian town for which Melania Trump helped broker a ceasefire
item.description: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a localised ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, an arrangement that will enable aid deliveries and allow evacuations from a frontline town suffering acute shortages of food and medicine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a localised ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, an arrangement that will enable aid deliveries and allow evacuations from a frontline town suffering acute shortages of food and medicine. The [USN:L1N46911P TEXT:"agreement"] was announced on October 23 and brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, with the additional involvement of Pope Leo, as Washington seeks to revive broader peace talks between Moscow and Kyiv. WHY ARE RESIDENTS OF OLESHKY AT RISK? Oleshky lies on the eastern bank of the Dnipro River in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, opposite Kherson city, which is held by Ukrainian forces. Russian troops seized Oleshky during the first days of their February 2022 invasion and have controlled it ever since. Oleshky has suffered extensive war damage and was hit hard by flooding after the destruction of the nearby Kakhovka dam in 2023. The United States has said only a few thousand people remain in Oleshky, from a prewar population of 24,000. Residents and officials have reported [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:"severe shortages of food"], medicine and other basic supplies. WHAT DOES THE CEASEFIRE INVOLVE? According to Ukrainian and Russian officials, the arrangement provides for a local halt in fighting, the delivery of humanitarian assistance and the evacuation of civilians who wish to leave the town. The two sides said humanitarian corridors would be established to allow aid deliveries and the movement of residents. WHO BROKERED THE DEAL? The White House said Melania Trump helped secure the agreement after becoming involved in discussions on the humanitarian situation in Oleshky. The White House said the first lady and a representative worked with Russian and Ukrainian officials to agree the terms of the ceasefire. Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets publicly thanked Melania Trump and her team for helping coordinate the talks. Russian officials also confirmed the agreement. [USN:L8N4651KU TEXT:"Pope Leo"] also played a role. He held a phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the Vatican said, and urged Ukraine and Russia to cooperate to let aid and food in. WHAT MIGHT HAPPEN NEXT? The ceasefire is limited in scope and does not address the wider conflict, now in its fifth year. But it is a rare example of direct cooperation between the two sides since the start of the invasion. The Kremlin said on Monday that the truce might serve as a precedent for similar localised ceasefires in the future.

item.title: SpaceX enters $40 billion deal with Apollo for AI chip financing
item.description: SpaceX said on Monday an affiliate of Apollo Global Management will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: SpaceX (SPCX.O) said on Monday an affiliate of Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion. Each lease will run a little over five years from the day the equipment arrives, according to a regulatory filing. The deal highlights SpaceX's heavy spending, as it tries to capitalize on surging demand for computing power to help bankroll its Moon and Mars ambitions. The company aims to finalize the deal by the end of the year. The leases are expected to start in the first half of 2027, once the chips are delivered. On Sunday, CEO Elon Musk said on X that SpaceX had [USN:L6N46B085 TEXT:""closed" $40 billion"] in debt financing for graphics processing units. Musk said the funding mainly targeted chips arriving in the first and second quarters and would not be "a major factor this quarter." CFO Bret Johnsen had said SpaceX still expects fourth-quarter capital expenditure of $35 billion to $40 billion. Reuters reported earlier this month that SpaceX was in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia (NVDA.O) chips.

item.title: Musk's grim outlook hits neoclouds as debt concerns mount
item.description: Shares of neocloud companies declined on Monday after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the sector could face consolidation and failures, adding to concerns over a widening gap between AI infrastructure investment and revenue generation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of neocloud companies declined on Monday after SpaceX CEO [USN:L6N46B085 TEXT:"Elon Musk said"] the sector could face consolidation and failures, adding to concerns over a widening gap between AI infrastructure investment and revenue generation. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , which has become a poster child for mounting concerns over heavy AI spending, declined 1.6%, while Nebius Group (NBIS.O) fell 4% and IREN (IREN.O) lost 1.5%. Shares of Applied Digital (APLD.O) shed 2%. In a social media post on Sunday, Musk said that neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, adding that SpaceX (SPCX.O) would not buy any neocloud companies, calling it "pointless". "200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many," he said. "Musk is correct. You're going to need another source of revenue and profits in order to finance these projects moving forward. The cost of capital is too high to make the returns attractive," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital in New York. In an email to Reuters, a CoreWeave spokesperson said that the company continues to see opportunities to finance its growth, underscored by qualities such as "differentiated technology". Musk was [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"not alone"] in flagging the risks to the sector. Earlier this month, research firm Gartner said CoreWeave was at the top of the 100-odd neoclouds most exposed to the increasing leverage, and added that 80% of the companies could cease independent operations by 2032. Some brokerages expect AI spending to shoot past a trillion dollars next year, adding to investor concerns about the repercussions of severe dependence on debt, at a time when AI assets face rapid depreciation and markets price in more interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. Bonds of Nebius maturing in 2034 and those of CoreWeave expiring in 2033 have hit record lows on the concerns. CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital and TeraWulf have reported quarterly losses over the past one year, while IREN has not turned a profit in the past three quarters, raising scrutiny over profitability. Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have fallen more than 30% this month alone. Investors betting on their fall have raked in at least [USN:L4N4681E0 TEXT:"$6 billion"] in paper profits.

item.title: Regeneron extends US agreement for additional supply of Ebola treatment
item.description: Regeneron said on Monday it extended its agreement with a US health authority to provide additional supply of its Ebola treatment, amid a growing outbreak in Africa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Regeneron (REGN.O) said on Monday it extended its agreement with a US health authority to provide additional supply of its Ebola treatment, amid a growing outbreak in Africa. Here are some details: The new agreement with the US Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, expanding a 2020 contract, will see Regeneron supply doses of its drug Inmazeb through 2031 for about $270 million The US Food and Drug Administration approved Inmazeb in 2020 for the treatment of infection caused by Zaire ebolavirus The current Ebola outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved specific antiviral treatment or licensed vaccine Regeneron said it is testing its experimental therapy, maftivimab, as a potential treatment for the Bundibugyo virus The outbreak, first reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May, has now spread to four countries across East, Central and West Africa — the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date The current outbreak has infected nearly 10,000 people and killed more than 4,800 in Congo The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding

item.title: Ovintiv to buy Logan Energy for $890 million, expanding Montney oil position
item.description: Oil and gas producer Ovintiv said on Monday it would acquire Canadian producer Logan Energy in an all-cash deal valuing the company at about $890 million, including debt.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oil and gas producer Ovintiv (OVV.N) said on Monday it would acquire Canadian producer Logan Energy (LGN.V) in an all-cash deal valuing the company at about $890 million, including debt. Here are more details: Ovintiv would pay C$1.40 ($0.9986) per share for Logan The deal would add about 266,000 net acres in the oil-rich Montney region and roughly 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day of production Ovintiv said the acquisition would add about 420 net drilling locations, including 220 premium-return wells The deal would also help generate annual cost synergies of roughly $60 million The deal is expected to close early in the first quarter of 2027 The assets include two oil batteries and stakes in two gas-processing facilities, which Ovintiv said should support margins and future production growth As part of the deal, Logan will spin off its newly formed subsidiary, Logan Oil Corp, to its shareholders Logan shareholders will also receive shares in spun-out Logan Oil Corp, initially valued at about C$0.08 per Logan share, and warrants, bringing total consideration to about C$1.48 per share In 2024, Ovintiv agreed to buy Paramount Resources' Montney assets for $2.38 billion while selling its Utah Uinta operations to FourPoint Resources for $2 billion ($1 = 1.4020 Canadian dollars)

item.title: Brasil tem menor saldo em transações correntes em 2 anos nos 12 meses até setembro
item.description: O déficit em transações correntes do Brasil diminuiu para 2,33% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) nos 12 meses até setembro, de 2,50% do PIB no mês anterior, mostraram dados do Banco Central nesta segunda-feira, atingindo o menor nível em dois anos, ajudado por um superávit comercial mais forte.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O déficit em transações correntes do Brasil diminuiu para 2,33% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) nos 12 meses até setembro, de 2,50% do PIB no mês anterior, mostraram dados do Banco Central nesta segunda-feira, atingindo o menor nível em dois anos, ajudado por um superávit comercial mais forte. Em setembro, as transações correntes da maior economia da América Latina registraram déficit de US$5,1 bilhões, enquanto economistas consultados em pesquisa da Reuters esperavam saldo negativo de US$5,0 bilhões. (BRCURA=ECI) Depois de aumentar acentuadamente em 2025, o déficit em transações correntes do Brasil acumulado em 12 meses vem apresentando melhora constante, apoiado por um superávit comercial crescente, impulsionado pela forte alta dos preços do petróleo, uma vez que o país é exportador líquido da commodity. O fortalecimento da balança comercial brasileira mais do que compensou o aumento dos déficits nas contas de serviços e de renda, que também apresentaram deterioração em setembro. O investimento direto no país (IDP) somou US$11,294 bilhões em setembro, superando amplamente os US$6,500 bilhões esperados pelos economistas na pesquisa da Reuters. (BRFDI=ECI) Nos 12 meses até setembro, o IDP subiu para 3,43% do PIB, ante 3,39% no mês anterior, permanecendo bem acima do déficit em transações correntes e indicando que os fluxos de capital de longo prazo continuaram financiando integralmente o déficit externo.

item.title: Senior doctors in England set to strike over pay offer in November
item.description: Senior hospital doctors in England are set to stage a two-day strike in November, the British Medical Association said on Monday, following a government recommendation of a below-inflation pay rise.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Senior hospital doctors in England are set to stage a two-day strike in November, the British Medical Association said on Monday, following a government recommendation of a below-inflation pay rise. The strike, due to take place on November 25 and 26, is the latest example of disputes over pay and working conditions across Britain's National Health Service which have led to more than a dozen rounds of industrial action since 2023. The government's proposal of a 2.4% rise to the body that sets doctors' pay for the 2027/2028 financial year, is a "significant real-terms pay cut by all current measures of inflation," the BMA said. It noted that senior doctors had seen a 25% cut to their pay in real terms over the last 17 years. The strike can be avoided if Britain's health minister commits to adequately funded formal negotiations on both pay and working conditions, the BMA said in a statement. The headline rate of CPI inflation in September was 3.5%, the Office for National Statistics said [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"on Wednesday"]. Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the BMA's decision was "very disappointing" following what she called constructive discussions between her department, the NHS and the BMA. "With colleagues across the NHS, I am determined to support staff and patients through the tough winter period," she said. "I hope the BMA will stay united with us in that effort, and not take irresponsible action that would place our health service under even greater pressure at this crucial time." The government had said in its evidence to the Review Body on Doctors' and Dentists' Remuneration, published on October 19, that its plan for a 2.4% rise did not have to make "trade offs against headline government health commitments".

item.title: FedEx appoints Jamere Jackson as chief financial officer
item.description: FedEx on Monday appointed Jamere Jackson as chief financial officer, effective November 30.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: FedEx (FDX.N) on Monday appointed Jamere Jackson as chief financial officer, effective November 30. Jackson will step down as CFO of AutoZone (AZO.N) on November 25. “During Jamere’s six-year tenure at AutoZone, he was a key contributor in helping shape the strategies we implemented to drive record sales, earnings," the automotive parts retailer's CEO Phil Daniele said. Jackson previously served as CFO of car rental firm Hertz (HTZ.O) and TV ratings company Nielsen. He also held senior finance roles at industrial giant General Electric (GE.N) and is a board member and audit committee chair at drugmaker Eli Lilly (LLY.N) . At FedEx, Jackson succeeds Claude Russ, who has been the interim finance chief since June 1, after John Dietrich [USN:L4N40W1MX TEXT:"stepped down"], following FedEx Freight's (FDXF.N) spinoff into a publicly traded company. FedEx is set to report third-quarter results on Wednesday.

item.title: Ukrainian who fled Oleshky views US-brokered ceasefire with deep scepticism
item.description: Six weeks ago, Vitaly, his wife Iryna, their 13-year-old son Vlad left the besieged town of Oleshky in Russian-occupied Ukraine to escape what they feared was certain death by starvation.
item.dc:creator: Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Six weeks ago, Vitaly, his wife Iryna, their 13-year-old son Vlad and their cat left the besieged town of Oleshky in Russian-occupied Ukraine to escape what they feared was certain death by starvation. Now back in Ukraine after a gruelling journey via Russia and Belarus, Vitaly views with deep scepticism a temporary ceasefire in his native town set to begin on Tuesday to allow evacuations and send in supplies. Russia and Ukraine reached the [USN:L1N4690MZ TEXT:"agreement"], announced by the White House on Friday, with the mediation of US first lady Melania Trump and after additional involvement from [USN:L8N4651KU TEXT:"Pope Leo"]. After more than four years living under Russian occupation in a town on the front line of fierce fighting with Ukrainian forces, Vitaly is not optimistic that the ceasefire can hold for long or the humanitarian situation significantly improve. "Regarding the truce, I'm very sceptical about all this," said Vitaly, 55, who declined to give his last name for security reasons because his relatives were still living in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. "I have a lot of respect for Melania Trump, but she does not influence dictator (Russian President Vladimir) Putin," he told Reuters, sitting in a modern apartment in the Kyiv region where his family has temporarily settled. He said many of those remaining in [USN:L2N46C0BA TEXT:"Oleshky"] are sick or elderly and it would be difficult for them to relocate. Ukraine and Russia blame each other for the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky. Drones present the greatest threat to civilian life, and the town is within easy reach of unmanned aerial vehicles belonging to both armies. Because supplies are running out and the route north is blocked by the Dnipro river, some residents have walked 20 km (12 miles) to the next village to stock up on food and water. The journey is fraught with danger and locals call it the [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:""road of death""]. TEMPORARY CEASEFIRE AGREED Ukraine and Russia agreed to a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky that is expected to begin on October 27 at 3 a.m. Kyiv time (0100 GMT). Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that Kyiv hoped it would be possible to open up Oleshky, provide access for food and medicine and allow people to leave the area. The Kremlin has said that all civilians wishing to leave Oleshky would be allowed to do so and that the evacuation was expected to take at least several days. Oleshky, a small town across the Dnipro from Ukraine's regional hub of Kherson, had a prewar population of some 24,000. It is still home to around 1,700 residents, including about 35 children, according to the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine. UNDER RUSSIAN CONTROL Russian troops have occupied Oleshky since the first days of the full-scale invasion in February 2022. It has been largely cut off from running water, electricity, gas and central heating since the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam in 2023 and subsequent flooding of nearby areas. As the war ground on, the humanitarian crisis deepened. By the middle of last year, the constant threat of drones choked off supply lines, causing food scarcity. And from late May this year, the situation became severe, according to residents Reuters has spoken to. Vitaly said his family survived for weeks by rationing a single cup of rice or buckwheat a day, occasionally adding a cucumber or tomato mixed with purslane, a common wild weed. During the summer months, some residents could sell vegetables, but prices were unaffordable for most. A kilo of tomatoes cost about 1,500 roubles ($18.50). To buy eggs, you needed to know the right people and 10 eggs would cost around 3,000 roubles, Vitaly recalled. No one was willing to sell potatoes. After counting their meagre food stocks, and remembering last winter when the temperature in their apartment dropped to between 1 and 3 degrees Celsius (34 and 37 degrees Fahrenheit), they decided to leave. "You look at what remained from your food supplies and realize that there is only one way for you — to go on foot or die of hunger," Vitaly said. Their home in Oleshky had been damaged by a drone, Iryna said, and they did not have anything left there. ARDUOUS ESCAPE On September 13, the family joined a small party of eight people and set out on foot. They walked for more than 20 km to the village of Radensk. The road was heavily mined, and drones were flying overhead. Vitaly said they saw the body of a woman lying on the road as they passed by. They took with them only their autumn clothes, Vlad's teddy bear, the cat and a handful of family photos. They travelled from Radensk by bus deeper into Russian-occupied Ukraine, crossed into Russia after lengthy questioning by authorities at the border, and finally Belarus before returning to Ukrainian-controlled territory on September 17. The family has spent the past several weeks settling into a new routine in the Kyiv region. One of their first purchases was a bag of potatoes, bought to cook mashed potatoes for their son. "The kid will be in school. We will be working. My wife needs to get her health back on track a bit," Vitaly said. As for his own future: "I will either join the army or will try to find a position somewhere here with weapon producers to help our country defeat its enemies."

item.title: Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise to fund AI expansion
item.description: Meta Platforms said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, as the social media giant spends aggressively on its AI infrastructure expansion.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Meta Platforms (META.O) said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, as the social media giant spends aggressively on its AI infrastructure expansion. The Facebook parent has launched public offerings worth about $35 billion in common and preferred stock, and said it also plans to launch a separate at-the-market share sale program worth up to $60 billion. The company will launch the larger share sale program after its new non-voting Class C shares begin trading, which is expected in the first quarter of 2027, but said it has not yet finalized its timing and terms of the sale. Meta's fundraising plan, among the biggest by an AI company, has also drawn interest of up to $5 billion in total from Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) for Class A shares. Their funding interest adds to concerns about an increasingly circular flow of capital in the AI industry, as chip suppliers help finance the expansion of one of their biggest customers. Meta has been pouring money into chips and data centers to compete better with OpenAI and Anthropic. "We expect investors to continue to question the financing and potential for future capital raises," William Blair analysts said in a note. "Overall, we believe the financing reinforces both Meta's confidence in the long-term returns from AI investment and the increasingly capital-intensive nature of pursuing that opportunity." The company's shares fell about 1.4% in morning trading. The latest fundraising further underscores a shift among big technology companies increasingly [USN:L6N3WU0Q5 TEXT:"tapping debt markets and raising equity"] to bolster their AI infrastructure, having previously relied on cash to fund their investments. Earlier this year, [USN:L4N42B1AK TEXT:"Alphabet increased the size"] of its equity offerings to $84.75 billion. Separately on Monday, SpaceX said an affiliate of Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of [USN:L6N46C0RJ TEXT:"about $40 billion"]. META'S AI SPENDING IS BURNING CASH Meta has committed to spend about $825 billion in the future, primarily driven by its growing investments in data centers, AI-related infrastructure and cloud computing power. But the aggressive expansion has eroded its historically strong free cash flow. The company reported a $2.12 billion cash burn in the third quarter, its first negative free cash flow in over a decade, compared with a positive cash flow of $10.63 billion a year ago. Still, the early popularity of [USN:L6N4500XV TEXT:"its consumer-focused AI agent Muse"] and release of a competitive new [USN:L4N45Y13Q TEXT:"series of AI models"] have helped partly justify Meta's aggressive investments. "We believe that Meta will ultimately produce a profitable AI business and its returns longer-term should help the company diversify, although the path may not be linear," William Blair analysts said. The company had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $82.45 billion and long-term debt of $80.92 billion as of September 30, according to its latest quarterly filing. Last week, Meta raised the lower end of its annual [USN:L4N4671S3 TEXT:"capital expenditure"] forecast to a range of $135 billion to $145 billion. The company has said it would issue Class C common stock in January 2027, effectively resulting in a two-for-one split, to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. Meta [USN:L6N46801B TEXT:"agreed to grant Zuckerberg Class C shares"] that he can sell to help pay a potential California billionaire wealth tax, in exchange for a commitment to keep him in California.

item.title: Verizon lifts annual forecasts, signs more than $2 billion AI infrastructure deal with AWS
item.description: Verizon raised its annual forecast for wireless subscriber additions on Monday, betting on strong demand for its simplified plans, and signed an AI infrastructure deal worth more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Verizon (VZ.N) raised its annual forecast for wireless subscriber additions on Monday, betting on strong demand for its simplified plans, and signed an AI infrastructure deal worth more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services. For the third quarter, the telecom carrier reported nearly double the analysts' estimate for gains in monthly-bill paying wireless subscribers at 406,000, against Visible Alpha expectations of 209,439. Verizon now expects to add between 1.1 million and 1.2 million postpaid phone subscribers this year compared with earlier projections of 750,000 to 1 million It also raised its full-year adjusted earnings per share forecast to $5.04 to $5.06, from $4.99 to $5.04 earlier However, third-quarter revenue of $34.3 billion fell short of analyst estimates of $34.74 billion, according to LSEG data Revenue was pressured by lower device upgrade volumes after Verizon began cutting device subsidies. Verizon expects this trend to continue in the fourth quarter. Verizon shares fell 2.5% in early trading Under its deal with Amazon's (AMZN.O) cloud unit, Verizon will provide high-capacity fiber-optic connectivity for AWS data centers CEO Dan Schulman said in the post-earnings call the company was in talks with additional hyperscalers, neocloud providers and large enterprise clients to supply dark or lit fiber connectivity Meanwhile, commenting on SpaceX’s (SPCX.O) plans to enter the mobile market, Schulman said building a competing terrestrial network would take four to six years and cost $300 billion to $500 billion Verizon would be "ferociously competitive" once SpaceX enters the market, he added

item.title: France's Macron promises 'strong measures' to assuage protests
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron promised on Monday that his government would announce a package of measures in response to weeks of street protests over a broad set of grievances, while acknowledging the risk of more unrest ahead.
item.dc:creator: Crispian Balmer, Sudip Kar-Gupta
item.content:encoded: French President Emmanuel Macron promised on Monday that his government would announce a package of measures in response to weeks of street protests over a broad set of grievances, while acknowledging the risk of more unrest ahead. His prime minister, Sebastien Lecornu, is set to hold a news conference after a meeting with unions of high school students who want more resources for the education sector and an overhaul of a university admissions process they say embeds inequalities. "I have ... asked the government to respond to the legitimate demands that lie at the root of this social movement," Macron told reporters in Marseille, where he travelled to inspect the damage from earlier protests. Macron repeated what Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said earlier, that more unrest is expected next weekend. FAR-RIGHT GANGS CONFRONT FAR-LEFT ACTIVISTS The protests show little sign of easing [USN:L1N46608H TEXT:"after violence"] nine days ago engulfed dozens of cities, leading to fears the state had lost control of the streets. In response to the turmoil, the interior ministry deployed 70,000 police for Saturday's demonstrations, which unions called to denounce the high cost of living and public services. The movement has grown far beyond initial student discontent, drawing in trade unions and "yellow vest" activists, known for their high-visibility jackets and mass demonstrations against economic pressures including high fuel costs. Nunez said the huge police presence prevented a repeat of violence seen earlier this month, but asked by BFM TV on Monday whether he expected further disturbances during [USN:L5N46B02K TEXT:"demonstrations planned"] for October 31, he replied: "Clearly, yes." "Halloween evening is traditionally always a bit lively. We expect it to be complicated again," he added. Nunez said 1,435 people were arrested nationwide during Saturday's demonstrations and said police had also recorded a new phenomenon, with organised far-right gangs confronting far-left activists in several cities. "We knew there had been calls from numerous identity-based and nationalist movements to come out, officially, to defend businesses," he said. "In a number of cities, such as Nice and Montpellier, these groups arrived in organised formations, mainly to target the ultra-left movement." The government sought to portray Saturday's operation as evidence it had regained the upper hand, despite sporadic violence, especially in France's three largest cities — Paris, Marseille and Lyon. "The state prevailed this weekend. The state was strong," government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon told RTL radio. She said protesters had raised legitimate grievances that needed to be heard, but added that restoring calm was a prerequisite for meaningful negotiations. With his presidential mandate due to expire in April and public finances under severe strain, Macron has limited scope to defuse the crisis through the costly concessions that helped quell previous waves of unrest. Business leaders said the unrest was continuing to inflict heavy economic damage despite a calmer weekend. Alain Di Crescenzo, head of the CCI France network of chambers of commerce and industry, said many retailers had remained closed as a precaution after the violence of October 17, adding that sales had fallen by about 80%. "We have shopkeepers who are tired and demoralised, and we are killing local commerce," he told Radio Classique.

item.title: EQT to buy Range Resources in $13 billion deal to create top US gas producer
item.description: EQT said on Monday it will buy Range Resources in a $13 billion all-stock deal to create the largest US natural gas producer, betting on rising demand from LNG exports and power generation.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Saha
item.content:encoded: EQT (EQT.N) said on Monday it will buy Range Resources (RRC.N) in a $13 billion all-stock deal to create the largest US natural gas producer, betting on rising demand from LNG exports and power generation. The deal combines two major Appalachian Basin producers, giving EQT greater scale and infrastructure to serve utilities, LNG exporters and industrial customers. Including debt, the combined company will have an enterprise value of more than $50 billion. US natural gas consumption is expected to hit record highs, driven by LNG exports and power demand from AI data centers. The Energy Information Administration forecasts domestic consumption to rise from 91.9 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 94.3 bcfd in 2027. EQT now expects potential Appalachian gas demand rising to 25 bcfd, compared with its previous estimate of 20 bcfd, CEO Toby Rice said on a conference call. The combined company will have net production of more than 9 billion cubic feet equivalent per day (bcfed), over 30 years of drilling inventory across nearly 3 million net acres and more than 3,700 miles of midstream infrastructure. Rival Expand Energy (EXE.O) produced about 7.2 bcfed in 2025 and expects output of 7.4-7.6 bcfed in 2026. Range shareholders will receive 0.987 EQT shares per share held, valuing the deal at $12.83 billion, or $54.91 per share, a 20.6% premium to Friday's closing price, according to a Reuters calculation. Shares of EQT were down 2.3%, while those of Range Resources were up 16.7% at $53.14. EQT shareholders will own about 73% of the combined company, while Range investors will hold the remaining 27%. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The combined company expects to generate about $20 billion in cumulative free cash flow over five years at recent market prices. The deal is also expected to lower EQT's unlevered free cash flow breakeven to below $2 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), helping it remain profitable through swings in natural gas prices. Rice said future production growth would be driven by customer demand rather than output targets, adding that mid-single-digit growth was achievable. EQT's management team will lead the combined company, which will retain its headquarters in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania. Two Range representatives, including CEO Dennis Degner, will join EQT's board.

item.title: Fans and players revel on frozen pond of ice hockey nostalgia
item.description: The Winnipeg Jets have a modern indoor arena but tens of thousands of their fans and those of the visiting Montreal Canadiens zipped up parkas, pulled on warm hats and stuffed their hands into mittens to watch their teams battle in a temporarily converted outdoor Canadian football stadium.
item.dc:creator: Ed White
item.content:encoded: The Winnipeg Jets have a modern indoor arena but tens of thousands of their fans and those of the visiting Montreal Canadiens zipped up parkas, pulled on warm hats and stuffed their hands into mittens to watch their teams battle in a temporarily converted outdoor Canadian football stadium. Sunday night's Heritage Classic was not just something different for fans of the National Hockey League's rare but popular outdoor ice hockey celebrations. It was an invitation to indulge in memories and emotions of a type of ice hockey that has bound millions of people to the fast-moving, hard-hitting Canadian sport. The Classic is always played in Canada, usually every two-to-three years, but other outdoor games are played in the US. "It's hockey in its purest form," said Jets captain Adam Lowry a day before the game. "We grew up envisioning playing in the NHL when we were playing on outdoor rinks or on frozen ponds. It's where you spent countless hours with your friends." "Super-excited. So much fun. It brings back great memories," said Jets forward Kyle Connor, whose family's choice of home when he was young was based on having enough room in the back yard for a good rink. In front of a sellout crowd of 32,343 the Jets could not deliver a home win for their fans on Sunday night, but the thousands wearing red Canadiens jerseys were able to celebrate a 2-1 victory in a unique setting. OUTDOOR RESURGENCE Millions of rural Canadians and Americans grew up playing the sport on frozen ponds on the family farm. Many more grew up in cities playing on backyard rinks built by their parents encouraging their kids to dream of glory. The Classic is avowedly nostalgic. Sunday's iteration was designed to evoke the feeling of cabin life from decades ago, with the areas of the field not covered by the rink containing fire pits surrounded by Adirondack chairs, pond-themed mini-rinks, and images of ice hockey heritage. Outdoor ice hockey is far from fading in Canada. There has been a boom in front-yard hockey rink construction turning residential areas into places where the slap and boom of sticks hitting pucks into boards, the swooshing of skates and the cheers of goal-scoring are now commonplace in the winter months. This resurgence comes as ice hockey faces growing concerns about a drop in interest and participation numbers in Canada amid escalating costs of equipment and increasing popularity of other sports. Canadian[USN:L8N43705T TEXT:" success in international"] soccer and the rise of prominent Canadian players in basketball and other globally watched sports have given children competing sporting dreams. However, for superfans Jack Kostaniuk, 9, and his brother William, 7, the Heritage Classic was a chance to meet their heroes. "Hey buddy!" said Jets and Canadiens players as they fist-bumped the brothers on their way to the outdoor rink for a Saturday practice. Jack's dad, Tim, said "we love this," about the outdoor event. His children sometimes play on outdoor rinks and they are now getting to see their favorite players do the same. TURMOIL AND TRADE The Heritage Classic came at a time when the Jets needed a lift after months of upheaval. Goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, a key factor in Winnipeg's success in recent years, publicly questioned the team's direction following the 2025-26 season and was suspended by the club after he did not report to training camp. On Friday, the Jets traded him to the New Jersey Devils in a deal that brought several players and draft picks to Winnipeg. After arriving from the Devils, Dawson Mercer has had little time to get to know his new teammates before being thrust into the spotlight of the marquee outdoor game. Despite some jitters, he was excited about jumping in at the deep end of his new home. "It's going to be a fun time. My family is in town, so that'll be exciting and definitely more of a welcoming event," said Mercer. Also in town were throngs of Montreal fans, many of whom flew thousands of kilometers to sit outside at near-freezing temperatures to cheer on their team. A group of warmly dressed Montreal-born fans now living in southern Ontario told Reuters the only reason they came for this match was because it was being held outside, and that sounded cool.

Meta said on Monday it [USN:L3N46C0RT TEXT:"plans to raise"] up to $95 billion in equity to fund its AI-related expansion of data centers, cloud computing power and other infrastructure. Its shares were last down 1.8%. The AI trade has come under pressure this month amid concerns that debt-funded spending may become harder to justify in the face of rising borrowing costs.
