item.title: US retailers face record holiday delivery prices from surcharges tied to costlier diesel
item.description: The most expensive parcel shipping year on record is on track to end with the highest-ever holiday season delivery prices as soaring diesel prices drive even higher fuel surcharge rates from UPS and FedEx , boosting costs for retailers.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Baertlein
item.content:encoded: The most expensive parcel shipping year on record is on track to end with the highest-ever holiday season delivery prices as soaring diesel prices drive even higher fuel surcharge rates from UPS (UPS.N) and FedEx (FDX.N) , boosting costs for retailers. Holiday-related package volume can double during the fourth quarter, when pricing for ground deliveries, including e-commerce purchases, is expected to be 5.8% higher than the same period last year, according to the TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index. Pricing for speedier express parcel deliveries is forecast to jump 13.8% from the fourth quarter of 2025, according to the index, which analyzes anonymized data from 1,800 shippers including major retailers. The index reports percentage change rather than dollar amounts because parcel costs vary based on weight, size and destination. "Fuel is front and center in everybody's consideration and, again, no real good news there," said Mingshu Bates, chief analytics officer at AFS Logistics. The US average on-highway diesel price was $6.28 per gallon as of October 19, according to the Energy Information Administration, up 65% since the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28. CHANGES TO CARRIERS' CALCULATIONS BOOST COSTS But diesel price increases account for just under 30% of the fuel surcharge cost, Bates said. Surcharges driven by changes to how industry leaders such as UPS and FedEx calculate them are rising far faster than fuel prices — and go up even when fuel prices do not, she said. For example, when diesel was $2.91 per gallon in the first quarter of 2021, the index fuel surcharge was 7.75% of the base shipping rate. Even if diesel returned to that price, the fuel surcharge now would be 23.75%, roughly three times higher, according to the index. That reflects how changes in fuel surcharge calculations are raising carriers' revenue and driving up retailers' costs. Based on company surcharge tables at the EIA's average diesel price of $6.28, UPS' fuel surcharge is 29.5% and FedEx's is 29%. UPS said its pricing reflects its premium service and infrastructure investments. FedEx did not immediately comment. The companies will report quarterly earnings this week and investors are keen to learn if customers are pushing back on surcharges. Fast-growing delivery firms, including OnTrac, GoFo, UniUni, Jitsu and Veho, cover some 70% of the US population and have added capacity to handle more volume during the holiday season, said Satish Jindel, president of ShipMatrix, a delivery tracking and management firm. "They are getting adoption from many shippers looking to lower their transportation spend," Jindel said. Nevertheless, some of those companies have also adopted hefty fuel surcharges. OnTrac's West Coast surcharge is 29.5% for the week ending October 25, according to the company's publicly available surcharge table. Retailers and other delivery customers could save money by shifting their business to the US Postal Service or to Amazon.com's (AMZN.O) logistics arm. The heavily regulated USPS imposed its first fuel surcharge of 8% on most packages in April, the same month Amazon began adding a 3.5% fuel and logistics-related surcharge to sellers' fulfillment fees. Switching deliveries between companies can bring downsides, analysts said. Splitting deliveries between firms can nullify any savings based on volume and holiday delivery plans are set months ahead, making late changes difficult, they said. To that end, JPMorgan analysts said it is unlikely Amazon will soon break UPS and FedEx's grip on the market.

item.title: Beware a boring UK budget that ages badly
item.description: Chancellor John Healey has talked markets into expecting little this autumn. Amid a £10 bln fiscal hole created by the Iran crisis, he may defer thorny spending decisions to 2027. But past budgets show how a calm reception can sour later, highlighting the risk of delay.
item.dc:creator: Jon Sindreu
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s ability to craft a narrative is on full display. To voters, he pitched radical policy changes addressing living costs and shifting decision-making locally. To "bond vigilantes," he looks to have sold a boring budget where little will be announced on October 28. The problem with plot holes is that criticism pours in later, when people mull them over. Burnham's finance minister John Healey is facing the same challenges as his predecessor Rachel Reeves. Her fiscal rules, designed to avoid a Liz Truss-style bond market revolt required day-to-day spending to balance and debt to fall relative to GDP years down the line. Yet after an initial high-tax budget in 2024, low growth made the "headroom" of £10 billion she had left over the deficit rule look paltry. She was forced not only to plug the gap by promising more revenue increases and spending cuts, but to raise it to £24 billion. Today, the situation has worsened again. The Iran war has pushed up borrowing costs, eating into those numbers. But based on what Healey has suggested, analysts don't expect him to rebuild the headroom, which is expected to come in between £10 billion and £15 billion on budget day. The fact that 10-year gilt yields have headed lower over the past two weeks implies the City of London also sees an energy shock as reasonable justification to eat into the cushion. Bank of America analysts break it down. Living-cost measures already announced by Burnham — including frozen bus fares and a 5% VAT cut on electricity — amount to £2 billion this fiscal year, and similar policies costing £13 billion until March 2028 could join them. Add £5 billion for defence over four years. That all means Healey may raise taxes by as much as £19 billion, Bank of America reckons, with banks likely among the targets. But compared to Reeves’ 2024 budget, designed to raise £40 billion annually, it's small potatoes. The budget may strike a balance consistent with Burnham's pattern of pairing large ambitions with low-key policies. But tough decisions will likely be kicked into the long grass. Tax increases are expected from 2028 onwards, and there's little indication so far that the Treasury is rushing to tackle much-needed welfare reform. Furthermore, Burnham has not yet spelled out how he will fund his plans to provide Brits with more old-age care. A bigger problem is that the current fiscal math contains a lot of unspecified back-loaded belt tightening. Government departments were already set to increase inflation-adjusted spending by only 1.3% yearly until 2031, compared to 2.5% over the past decade. Add the recent cost surge and it falls to 1%. Government hopes that productivity gains will fill the gap look extremely optimistic. Healey can avoid details for now, but he must still explain how exactly they are supposed to happen in the Spending Review next year. Market sentiment can be a double-edged sword. Healey should remember that, even if a budget initially gets the green light from investors, they can later reassess the whole affair. This is exactly what happened to Reeves, who initially got a warm reception to her 2024 budget only to scramble to cater to investors' narrow focus on the shrinking headroom in 2025. Storytelling is ultimately no replacement for credible plans. Follow Jon Sindreu on X and LinkedIn . British Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey is due to present the government's Autumn Budget on October 28. Rising European oil and gas prices have raised concerns that higher energy-related spending and weaker growth could reduce the Treasury's fiscal headroom against its borrowing rules. Official data published on October 21 showed that public sector borrowing in the year to September was £97.8 billion, which is 4.3% less than in the same period of last year but 6.5% more than was expected by the United Kingdom's independent fiscal watchdog, the Office for Budget Responsibility, in its March forecasts. The UK government will issue debt to give £20.4 billion of additional support to the National Wealth Fund (NWF) and British Business Bank (BBB), the Financial Times published on October 24 citing the Treasury. As of 0900 GMT on October 26, Britain's 10-year government bond yields traded at 5.3588%, compared with 5.3656% at the close on October 23. Most benchmark yields from peer countries were up at the time. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: US singer Chris Brown spared jail for UK nightclub attack
item.description: US singer Chris Brown was spared an immediate prison sentence in Britain on Monday for attacking a music producer with a tequila bottle in a London nightclub in 2023, with his fans cheering as the musician walked free from court.
item.dc:creator: Sam Tobin
item.content:encoded: US singer Chris Brown was spared an immediate prison sentence in Britain on Monday for attacking a music producer with a tequila bottle in a London nightclub in 2023, with his fans cheering as the musician walked free from court. Brown, 37, was given an eight-month suspended sentence at London's Southwark Crown Court over the attack on Abraham Diaw at the Tape nightclub in February 2023 that lasted around 20 seconds. Diaw was hit twice in the head with a bottle, which was then swung twice more at him in what prosecutors described as "a vicious and unprovoked attack". The R&B star and his vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu, 40, [USN:L8N43Q128 TEXT:"pleaded guilty"] to a charge of affray in July, having denied more serious charges of [USN:L8N3SN0EY TEXT:"attempting"] to inflict grievous bodily harm and [USN:L8N3T80KH TEXT:"assault"] causing actual bodily harm. NO SPECIAL TREATMENT Judge Tony Baumgartner said: "This was serious, public violence. In your case, Brown, it involved the repeated use ... of a bottle, including twice striking Diaw to his head." The judge told Brown: "Your fame, commercial success and professional standing do not entitle you to special treatment – the law applies equally to everyone." But Baumgartner said he could suspend Brown's sentence for 12 months, meaning he will not go to prison unless he commits another offence in that period. Akinlolu was also spared an immediate jail sentence. "Violence will not be accepted on the streets of London," Detective Chief Superintendent Christina Jessah from the Metropolitan Police said in a statement. "Regardless of an individual's profile or status, we will pursue those responsible and work tirelessly to bring them before the courts." BROWN'S FANS CHEER SUSPENDED SENTENCE Brown, winner of Grammy awards for best R&B album in 2011 and 2025, has previously admitted other violent offences in the US, having been [USN:TRE52464A TEXT:"charged"] with assaulting his then-partner, singer Rihanna, in 2009, with a photo of her bruised face making headlines around the world. Prosecutor Heidi Stonecliffe said Brown pleaded guilty to the 2009 assault of Rihanna and was sentenced to five years' probation. He also admitted a [USN:KBN0GX1HN TEXT:"2013 assault"] on a fan he was accused of punching when he asked for a photograph. Brown remains hugely popular and has sold tens of millions of records worldwide, with dozens of fans queuing outside court from around 0700 GMT, about an hour before the building opened. His lawyer Sallie Bennett-Jenkins said Brown was profoundly sorry for the incident and described him as "a dedicated, loving and loyal father to four children". "This was an ugly and unattractive incident, we would be the first to accept," she added. "It was, however, an incident that was very short-lived." Brown thanked the judge before leaving the dock and nodding towards about two dozen of his supporters in the public gallery. Other fans who gathered outside the building cheered as Brown left and went into a waiting car. Brown was arrested in May 2025 having returned to Britain for the first time since the attack and was initially [USN:L8N3RO0X2 TEXT:"denied"] bail, throwing his worldwide "Breezy Bowl XX" tour into doubt. But Brown was eventually [USN:L8N3RT0WH TEXT:"released"] after promising to pay a £5 million ($6.7 million) security fee, allowing the tour to go ahead. ($1 = 0.7487 pounds)

item.title: Japan auto union group looks beyond inflation-linked pay hikes for 2027 talks
item.description: Japan's top automobile industry union group is looking to move beyond wage demands aimed merely at keeping pace with inflation in next year's labour talks, as stronger pay growth is needed to help ensure that it has the skilled workers to compete with the challenge from China, its chief said.
item.dc:creator: Makiko Yamazaki, Kentaro Sugiyama
item.content:encoded: Japan's top automobile industry union group is looking to move beyond wage demands aimed merely at keeping pace with inflation in next year's labour talks, as stronger pay growth is needed to help ensure that it has the skilled workers to compete with the challenge from China, its chief said. "We are discussing raising the bar compared with previous years" for the 2027 spring wage talks, Akihiro Kaneko, president of the Confederation of Japan Automobile Workers' Unions (JAW), told Reuters in an interview on Monday. After securing the strongest wage gains in decades in recent years, JAW believes annual pay hikes focused primarily on protecting workers from rising living costs are no longer sufficient to reverse decades of wage stagnation, Kaneko said. Instead, he argued that wages should increasingly reflect gains in productivity and the value created by workers, helping Japan narrow the gap with overseas competitors. Kaneko said the Japanese automobile industry faces an increasingly tough operating environment due to the rapid rise of Chinese automakers, particularly in electric vehicles. Rather than engaging in a losing battle on costs with China, however, Japan should focus on developing higher-value products through investment in people, he said. JAW has 12 unions under its umbrella, representing a total of 780,000 workers, including those of Toyota Motor (7203.T) , Honda Motor (7267.T) , and parts makers. JAW's member unions secured an average monthly wage increase of 4.81% in this year's labour talks, including base-pay hikes of 3.58%. That compared with overall wage growth of 4.94%, including base-pay increases of 3.58%, a year earlier. Last year, Japan's core consumer inflation averaged 3.1%. While it remained below the Bank of Japan's 2% target for much of this year, it [USN:L4N46724Q TEXT:"accelerated"] to 2.1% in September, topping the target for the first time in nine months. Japan's automobile industry, broadly responsible for the employment of 5.5 million people, typically sets the tone for the country's wage negotiations that swing into full gear in the first few months of the year. Japan's largest labour union group Rengo, to which JAW belongs, last week [USN:P8N45S026 TEXT:"unveiled"] a more ambitious wage bargaining policy for next year's annual labour negotiations, setting a target centred at a pay hike of 6% while maintaining a minimum benchmark of 5% or more.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nigeria's Ebola patient left the country on a medical evacuation flight to Switzerland on Monday morning, the health minister said, adding that her clinical condition was much improved. The patient, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, is Nigeria's [USN:L1N4690CW TEXT:"first Ebola case"] in more than a decade. The outbreak, which started in Democratic Republic of Congo, has now been reported in four countries in East, Central and West Africa, giving it the [USN:L1N4690CW TEXT:"widest geographic spread"] of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date. The possibility that the Nigerian patient became infected in Uganda, where officials say she spent a two-week holiday before returning to Abuja, has fuelled concerns about undetected transmission in a country where the outbreak had appeared to be under control. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said in a post on X that the woman was "stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline" before her evacuation flight departed. Her spouse has remained asymptomatic and left Nigeria on the same flight, Pate added. The Swiss foreign ministry and Uganda's health ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. SCIENTISTS INVESTIGATING HOW PATIENT CAUGHT RARE STRAIN A team of leading Ebola scientists will travel to Nigeria to help investigate how the patient caught the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya [USN:L6N46C0FF TEXT:"told Reuters in an interview"]. Switzerland said last week that she had not travelled to Congo, contradicting statements from Ugandan officials. Her travel documents show she had not visited Congo, Kaseya said. There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo species, which has now caused almost 10,000 cases and more than 4,800 deaths in Congo, and spread to three other countries in Africa – Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda. Kenya has reported nine cases and two deaths, all linked to a man who had travelled from Congo via Uganda's Entebbe airport. Uganda reported 20 cases in May and June but has not recorded any since and was declared free of the virus by the World Health Organization in August. The WHO's Africa director congratulated Nigeria's government and health workers for stabilising the patient's condition, allowing her to be evacuated. "The Nigerian medical team successfully managed her through the acute phase of the illness and stabilized her condition," Mohamed Janabi said on X.

item.title: Audi CEO faces backlash after joining Trump at midterm campaign rally
item.description: Audi chief Gernot Doellner drew heavy criticism on Monday for appearing alongside US President Donald Trump at a campaign rally in the battleground state of Georgia, with the head of Germany's top union saying it violated the automaker's company guidelines.
item.dc:creator: Rachel More, Christina Amann
item.content:encoded: Audi chief Gernot Doellner drew heavy criticism on Monday for appearing alongside US President Donald Trump at a campaign rally in the battleground state of Georgia, with the head of Germany's top union saying it violated the automaker's company guidelines. Doellner appeared alongside Trump at the rally in Perry, near Macon in central Georgia, to announce plans to build a $4 billion plant, the luxury carmaker's first in the US, which would produce 200,000 SUVs annually. TOP VW COMMITTEE MUST DECIDE ON US PLANT The announcement of the plan, which needs approval by the supervisory board of parent Volkswagen , including German labour representatives, follows lengthy considerations over launching US production to escape import tariffs that cost Audi around €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) last year. "Doellner is also in flagrant breach of his own company's rules, which expressly require political neutrality in the run-up to elections," said Christiane Benner, head of Germany's IG Metall union and deputy chair of Volkswagen's supervisory board. Audi had no immediate comment on the matter. However, a person familiar with the matter said Audi's management board had cleared an exception to the company's code of conduct before Doellner's appearance. Under the code, the board can allow deviations from the rules except in cases involving criminal offences, the source said. The automaker's top stakeholders discussed the matter during a meeting attended by Benner and another labour representative Daniela Cavallo, with the latter expressing reservations about the appearance without formally opposing it, the person said. "From a pure business perspective, localising Audi's production in the US may make sense," Cavallo said in comments shared internally and seen by Reuters. However, with his appearance, Doellner "allowed himself to be turned into a puppet in the propaganda show" of Trump, she said. A second person confirmed that Volkswagen's supervisory board committee — which is already fraught with tension over the company's [USN:L8N4690LO TEXT:"sweeping restructuring"] — had discussed the issue on Friday. Trump has voiced his support in the past for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, raising concerns among Germany's political and corporate mainstream. German automotive expert Ferdinand Dudenhoeffer referred to Doellner as a "mini Elon Musk", comparing him to the Tesla boss who has appeared on stage with Trump. Audi's code of conduct forbids "public engagements with political parties or politicians standing for election, nor any sponsorship of such events" in the three months leading up to an election. TRUMP KEEN TO PROMOTE IMPACT OF TARIFFS Trump is in the midst of a nationwide campaign blitz to bolster his Republicans, who are trailing the Democrats in opinion polls ahead of the November 3 midterm elections . One of his campaign messages is that his tariffs are creating more US manufacturing jobs. Olaf Lies, state premier of the German state of Lower Saxony, Volkswagen's second-largest shareholder, said it was inappropriate that Doellner had become part of a political spectacle. "A campaign rally cannot be the right place to announce an investment of this magnitude," he said. "This appearance has caused consternation among employees who are worried about their jobs here, and far beyond. I can fully understand that — I feel the same way." The US investment plan coincides with Volkswagen's push to cut around 100,000 jobs and cut excess production as it grapples with heavy losses in China while absorbing steep tariffs and the costly transition to electric vehicles. The group's German production sites have been under particular pressure to reduce costs, with Audi's factory in Neckarsulm one of four plants threatened with closure from early next decade. "The optics are not great, jobs are being created in the US while Audi is reducing the capacity globally," Metzler analysts said of the US plan. "Still, we would argue the decision to produce in the US is right." ($1 = 0.8925 euros)

item.title: Galp, Moeve scrap downstream merger as Iran war boosts refinery valuations
item.description: Portugal's Galp Energia and Spain's Moeve called off a merger of their downstream assets on Monday as the US-Iran war turns refineries around the world from struggling businesses into prized assets, making long-term valuations for mergers extremely difficult.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Pietro Lombardi
item.content:encoded: Portugal's Galp Energia (GALP.LS) and Spain's Moeve called off a merger of their downstream assets on Monday as the US-Iran war turns refineries around the world from struggling businesses into prized assets, making long-term valuations for mergers extremely difficult. Galp and Moeve – formerly known as Cepsa and owned by Abu Dhabi's Mubadala and US investment firm Carlyle (CG.O) – announced a [USN:L6N3Y90KL TEXT:"non-binding agreement"] in January to explore merging some of their assets through two joint ventures. One source familiar with the talks said volatility on energy markets sparked by the Iran war made it difficult to put a value on the refineries, adding that there is no intention of resuming talks in the mid-term. Galp co-CEO Joao Diogo Marques da Silva said on a call with analysts that the decision to abandon talks with Moeve came at the "last mile" but it was "nonetheless a well-supported one as the commercial terms didn't allow us to reach a sustainable and value-creative deal". "No deal is better than a bad deal ... we are really comfortable with the quality of the assets that we hold", he said, highlighting the strong results delivered by the company. EARNINGS BOOSTED BY RECORD REFINING MARGINS He said it remained part of Galp's strategy "to segregate the commercial retail business from the industrial business", but that there was "no pressure whatsoever to have a transaction" with a partner. Moeve CEO Maarten Wetselaar said in a statement the company remained "fully focused" on its strategic transformation towards low-carbon businesses. Galp also reported a 67% rise in third-quarter [USN:L5N46B072 TEXT:"adjusted core profit"] to €1.52 billion ($1.7 billion), beating expectations on the back of record refining margins. The Portuguese group joined a string of global peers reporting [USN:L6N4600WB TEXT:"bumper earnings"] as fuel supply disruptions due to war in Iran pushed diesel, gasoline and other refined-product prices higher relative to crude, boosting refining margins worldwide. GALP SHARES DROP Its unit that includes the Sines refinery was the second-largest contributor, with core profit more than doubling to €639 million in the quarter as refining margins more than tripled year-on-year to $33.8 per barrel from $9.5 a year earlier, and doubled from $16.8 in the preceding quarter. Moeve has yet to report its third-quarter earnings, but in the second quarter its energy business, which includes its refineries, nearly doubled adjusted core profit to €541 million, while refining margins rose to $11.3 per barrel, almost twice the level recorded a year earlier. The collapse of the talks leaves Galp's refining, chemicals and fuel-retail businesses under its sole ownership, while the group continues to focus on its core growth areas, including oil production in Brazil and renewable energy. A separate industrial venture would have combined Galp's Sines refinery with Moeve's Huelva and Algeciras refineries, creating a refining platform with crude processing capacity of about 700,000 barrels per day. The companies had also planned to create a retail business operating around 3,500 service stations, primarily in Spain and Portugal. Galp shares fell 9.5% in afternoon trading. RBC analysts said investors had expected a Moeve-Galp deal early in the fourth quarter, believing it would eliminate a major obstacle to a potential takeover of Galp in future. They said the lack of a deal "may call into question Galp's premium valuation relative to peers". ($1 = 0.8925 euros)

item.title: Irán recibe a países del pacto de defensa saudí mientras hutíes lanzan nuevos ataques
item.description: Altos cargos de Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán tenían previsto llegar a Irán el lunes en un intento por rebajar la tensión del conflicto regional que afecta al reino, mientras los hutíes de Yemen lanzaban nuevos ataques contra el aeropuerto de Riad y las instalaciones petroleras saudíes.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills, Ariba Shahid, Menna Alaaeldin
item.content:encoded: Altos cargos de Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán tenían previsto llegar a Irán el lunes en un intento por rebajar la tensión del conflicto regional que afecta al reino, mientras los hutíes de Yemen lanzaban nuevos ataques contra el aeropuerto de Riad y las instalaciones petroleras saudíes. Las conversaciones serán el primer contacto de alto nivel entre Irán y las tres naciones —que firmaron en agosto el pacto de defensa mutua de La Meca— desde que la guerra, que comenzó con ataques estadounidenses e israelíes contra Irán, se extendiera también a Arabia Saudita y Yemen. El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores saudí afirmó que la visita forma parte de los esfuerzos para "desescalar" y "promover el diálogo y las soluciones diplomáticas". Asimismo, subrayó la necesidad de abrir canales de negociación para "evitar que se reanude la escalada militar". Arabia Saudita estará representada por el ministro de Defensa, el príncipe Jalid bin Salman, hermano menor del príncipe heredero Mohammed bin Salman; Pakistán, por el jefe del Ejército, el mariscal de campo Asim Munir; y Turquía, por el jefe de los servicios de inteligencia, Ibrahim Kalin, según fuentes oficiales saudíes e iraníes. Tenían previstas consultas con el Consejo Supremo de Seguridad Nacional de Irán, según declaró su vicesecretario, Ali Baqeri-Kani, a la televisión estatal. Pakistán y Qatar han liderado los esfuerzos de mediación en la guerra. Mediadores qataríes se encontraban en Teherán el domingo, según informó un funcionario a Reuters. Los esfuerzos anteriores contribuyeron a alcanzar un acuerdo de paz provisional en junio, pero los combates entre Irán y Estados Unidos se reanudaron poco después. Posteriormente, estalló el conflicto entre los hutíes, alineados con Irán, y Arabia Saudita, aliada de Estados Unidos, lo que abrió un nuevo frente. La ampliación de los combates ha restringido el tráfico marítimo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, punto estratégico para el transporte de energía, ha disparado los precios mundiales del petróleo y el gas, ha dejado a los países del golfo Pérsico expuestos a ataques con misiles y drones, y ha provocado una nueva crisis humanitaria en Yemen. Las tensiones entre Washington y Teherán se han agudizado en los últimos días. El presidente Donald Trump afirmó el viernes que podría llevar a cabo otra operación militar contra Irán. Funcionarios de seguridad iraníes indicaron a Reuters que Teherán ha elaborado planes detallados para atacar los cables submarinos del golfo Pérsico si Estados Unidos e Israel vuelven a atacar. La guerra, que a principios de año también reavivó los combates entre Israel y el grupo armado libanés Hezbolá, respaldado por Irán, ha lastrado los índices de popularidad de Trump de cara a las elecciones de mitad de legislatura que decidirán el control del Congreso. El portavoz del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores iraní, Esmaeil Baghaei, dijo que la cita versará sobre "las políticas expansionistas de Israel, la evolución de la situación en los territorios palestinos y en Líbano, y las repercusiones de la acción militar de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán". Baghaei señaló que la reunión, propuesta cuando Munir visitó Teherán la semana pasada, podría ser un primer paso hacia el establecimiento de mecanismos de seguridad regionales. Un alto funcionario de seguridad paquistaní afirmó que el objetivo es crear una red regional de no agresión. La agenda incluye también las conversaciones entre Washington y Teherán, los ataques hutíes contra Arabia Saudita, el estrecho de Ormuz y el bloqueo estadounidense de los puertos iraníes, según el funcionario. Los medios iraníes indicaron que las autoridades comunicaron a Munir que no habrá conversaciones con Washington hasta que no se cumplan exigencias como el fin del bloqueo estadounidense y el levantamiento de las sanciones sobre las exportaciones de petróleo iraní. ATAQUES DE LOS HUTÍES Riad ha intensificado los ataques contra los hutíes desde que capturaron zonas estratégicas a lo largo de la costa yemení del mar Rojo el mes pasado. Los ataques hutíes han tenido como objetivo aeropuertos, puertos e instalaciones petroleras saudíes. Los hutíes afirmaron el lunes que habían atacado estaciones de bombeo de crudo Este-Oeste en Arabia Saudita, así como el aeropuerto de Riad, que había anunciado que había reanudado las operaciones en dos terminales el día anterior. No hubo confirmación inmediata por parte saudí. El Acuerdo de Defensa Conjunta de La Meca establece que los signatarios utilizarán "todos los medios necesarios" para eliminar las amenazas a la integridad territorial, la soberanía o las fronteras internacionalmente reconocidas de cada uno de ellos, según un texto al que tuvo acceso Reuters. Los miembros del pacto celebraron una reunión de emergencia en Riad este mes y acordaron garantizar el "rápido despliegue" de fuerzas y capacidades militares en Arabia Saudita . Los trámites del Parlamento turco para ratificar el acuerdo comenzaron la semana pasada y aún están en curso, mientras que Pakistán aprobó el pacto la semana pasada.

item.title: Acciones y moneda de Brasil se hunden; reelección de Lula termina con racha alcista
item.description: Las acciones brasileñas y el real sufrían una fuerte caída tras la inesperada reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, lo que provocó la disipación del optimismo inversor que había surgido tras el éxito de su rival de derecha en la primera vuelta electoral.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres, Karin Strohecker
item.content:encoded: Las acciones brasileñas y el real sufrían una fuerte caída tras la inesperada reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, lo que provocó la disipación del optimismo inversor que había surgido tras el éxito de su rival de derecha en la primera vuelta electoral. El real brasileño se depreciaba cerca de un 12% frente al dólar en el mercado al contado al inicio de la jornada -uno de los mayores movimientos registrados- mientras que el referencial bursátil (.BVSP) se desplomaba más de un 16% y los futuros de las tasas de interés anotaban un fuerte incremento. La oleada de ventas afectó también a los bonos soberanos brasileños en los mercados internacionales; los títulos a más largo plazo fueron los más perjudicados, con la deuda con vencimiento en 2056 cayendo alrededor de 2,5 centavos. La bolsa brasileña detuvo sus operaciones durante 30 minutos después de que el índice de referencia Bovespa (.BVSP) cayera un 10% respecto a su cierre anterior, lo que activó el mecanismo de interrupción automática del mercado, informó en un comunicado B3, el operador bursátil. Los "credit default swaps" (CDS) a cinco años de Brasil, un indicador del costo de asegurarse contra un impago soberano, subieron hasta los 151,67 puntos básicos, frente a los 120,21 puntos del cierre del viernes, según datos de S&P Global Market Intelligence. Ante el desplome de los mercados brasileños, el Tesoro nacional canceló las subastas programadas de bonos gubernamentales, tanto los vinculados a la inflación como los de tasa fija, previstas para el 27 y el 29 de octubre, respectivamente. El colapso supone un giro drástico respecto a la tendencia alcista este mes, cuando los mercados subieron ante la expectativa de un viraje hacia la derecha, después de que Flávio Bolsonaro, hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, obtuvo inesperadamente el primer lugar en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales. El viernes, el índice Bovespa cerró casi un 7% por encima de su nivel previo a la primera vuelta, mientras que el real se había fortalecido cerca de un 5% frente al dólar. Los futuros de las tasas de interés también reflejaban la expectativa de que una política fiscal más restrictiva, bajo un eventual gobierno de Flávio Bolsonaro, permitiría una reducción en los costos de endeudamiento. La negativa del senador Bolsonaro a reconocer su derrota y su promesa de buscar la anulación de los resultados han aumentado la incertidumbre entre los inversores. "Un factor clave para los mercados financieros locales será la rapidez con la que Bolsonaro acepte el resultado, o al menos permita que el proceso constitucional siga su curso", afirmó Chris Turner, estratega de ING en Londres. Ahora, la atención se centrará en la elección de Lula para el cargo de ministro de Hacienda y en lo que esto revele sobre su enfoque fiscal. "La señal fundamental para los mercados será el compromiso de la futura administración de Lula con la disciplina fiscal, empezando por el nombramiento de un nuevo ministro de Hacienda en las próximas semanas", indicó Graham Stock, de RBC BlueBay Asset Management. DESAFÍOS Lula se enfrenta al reto de frenar el aumento de la deuda de Brasil, al tiempo que protege los programas sociales y la inversión. Los inversores buscan indicios de que su enfoque fiscal gradualista pueda reducir los costos de endeudamiento. "La administración de Lula no tendrá más remedio que llevar a cabo cierta consolidación fiscal, pero la mayoría de los inversores duda de que sea suficiente para encarrilar de nuevo la sostenibilidad de la deuda", comentó Thierry Larose, gestor de carteras en Vontobel Asset Management. Si no existe la confianza de que Lula pueda cumplir sus objetivos, los prestamistas podrían exigir tipos de interés más elevados, lo que aumentaría la carga de la deuda brasileña y encarecería el crédito para empresas y hogares. "Los inversionistas quieren un compromiso claro y creíble con la disciplina fiscal", dijo Alejo Czerwonko, director de inversiones para mercados emergentes de UBS Global Wealth Management. "Prevemos que el repunte que siguió a la primera vuelta ya esté en gran medida descontado en los precios, y que el ánimo se mantenga débil hasta que surja un plan fiscal claro". Czerwonko señaló que los inversionistas esperan que se ponga fin al gasto que acompañó a la campaña y que se trace una vía creíble para estabilizar la deuda pública. "Esto también implica una relación de trabajo con un Congreso de tendencia opositora, ya que ningún plan fiscal se aprueba sin él", añadió. El equipo de Lula se propone alcanzar un superávit presupuestario primario de alrededor del 1,3% del producto interno bruto para 2030. Eso dejaría fondos para cubrir parte de los intereses, reduciendo la necesidad de nuevos préstamos. Sin embargo, la deuda pública ya supera el 82% del PIB, mientras que las pensiones y otros gastos obligatorios por ley limitan las fuentes de ahorro. "Las políticas de Lula han hablado de recortes de gasto, pero no ha entrado en detalles sobre cómo se concretarán", señaló Divya Singaravelu, directora de investigación de Meridian 1305 Capital.

item.title: Gold rises as lower oil prices ease inflation fears ahead of Fed meeting
item.description: Gold prices rose on Monday, rebounding from the previous session's over three-month low, as retreating oil prices tempered inflation concerns ahead of this week's US Federal Reserve meeting.
item.dc:creator: Noel John
item.content:encoded: Gold prices rose on Monday, rebounding from the previous session's over three-month low, as retreating oil prices tempered inflation concerns ahead of this week's US Federal Reserve meeting. Spot gold rose 0.3% to $4,007.57 per ounce by 9:23 a.m. EDT (1323 GMT) after hitting $3,975 on Friday, its lowest level since July 20. US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.4% to $4,021.80 per ounce. "There's been a bit of a pullback in crude oil, which is helping gold, while some bargain-hunting is also coming in," said Bob Haberkorn, senior market strategist at StoneX. "I think it's going to be light trading here and we're going to hang around the $4,000 level into the Fed announcement to see what they have to say." Oil prices fell after surging last week but still held near six-month highs, amid hopes of easing hostilities between the US and Iran. The pullback in oil has offered some relief to inflation concerns, though markets remain wary of renewed supply disruptions that could reignite price pressures. The Fed's rate decision is due on Wednesday, with a pause widely expected after its September hike, while expectations for a December rate-hike are at 82%, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool. FEDWATCH Higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold. Fed policymakers have telegraphed they [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"will not raise US short-term borrowing"] costs again this week, but with inflation concerns still front and centre, investors believe a rate-hike pause will not last for long. Investors also await US Personal Consumption Expenditures data due on Thursday, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, for fresh clues on the interest-rate outlook. Attention is also turning to the November 3 US midterm elections, with investors assessing how the outcome could affect fiscal policy and broader market sentiment. "We would focus less on the (election) result itself and more on what it implies for fiscal policy, tariffs, geopolitical spending and policy uncertainty. These may have implications for US Treasury yields, dollar and gold," analysts at OCBC said in a note. Among other metals, spot silver was down 0.4% at $53.67 per ounce, platinum slid 1% to $1,534.80, while palladium rose 0.4% to $1,048.37.

item.title: Rybakina finds Ningbo spark again ahead of WTA Finals title defence
item.description: A year after winning the Ningbo Open transformed Elena Rybakina's season, the world number one returned to the Chinese city and retained her title on Sunday, as her game clicked into gear before another tilt at the WTA Finals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A year after winning the Ningbo Open transformed Elena Rybakina's season, the world number one returned to the Chinese city and retained her title on Sunday, as her game clicked into gear before another tilt at the WTA Finals. Her 2025 success proved the springboard for a stellar run as she secured the last spot in the eight-player WTA Finals field the following week, before winning the season finale and carrying that momentum into the current campaign. The 27-year-old Kazakh went on to capture the Australian Open title in January before claiming her third Grand Slam crown at the US Open last month. Rybakina's 6-2 6-2 win over Leylah Fernandez in the [USN:L2N46B01T TEXT:"Ningbo final"] on Sunday came after she had suffered defeat in her first match as world number one in Beijing and an injury-enforced absence from Wuhan. "It's the first time I've defended a title, so it's a great achievement," Rybakina told the WTA website. "Ningbo is already a special place. Last year I started to play really well from this tournament. Hopefully it's going to give me motivation and good energy to continue this season and start the next one." After losing nine of her first 13 finals, Rybakina has now won 11 of her last 15. "I remember I was getting upset always losing in finals," she said after winning her fourth title of the year and 15th overall. "Now it's going my way, but I can't expect it all the time ... now it's experience clicking in important moments." Rybakina plays in the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo this week before heading to Indian Wells for the November 8-15 WTA Finals, where she went unbeaten last year to pocket over $5 million in prize money.

item.title: Brazil stocks, real tumble as Lula win ends bullish run
item.description: Brazilian stocks and the real currency slumped after the surprise reelection of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as the bullish investor sentiment which followed his right-wing rival's success in the first round of voting evaporated.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres, Karin Strohecker
item.content:encoded: Brazilian stocks and the real currency slumped after the surprise [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"reelection"] of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as the bullish investor sentiment which followed his right-wing rival's success in the first round of voting evaporated. Brazil's real , tumbled nearly 12% against the US dollar in early spot trading, one of its biggest daily moves on record, while [USN:S0N45R008 TEXT:"Bovespa stock index futures"] fell nearly 15% and interest rate futures rose. The selloff hit Brazil's [USN:L5N46C0GQ TEXT:"sovereign debt"], with longer-dated bonds hit hardest and the 2056 maturity down around 2.5 cents. Meanwhile, trading on Brazil's stock exchange was halted for 30 minutes after the benchmark Bovespa index fell 10% from its last close, triggering the market's circuit breaker mechanism, stock exchange operator B3 said in a statement. The move came after B3 initially expanded the daily trading limits for Bovespa stock index futures, dollar futures and interest rate futures in response to heightened market volatility. Brazil's five-year credit default swaps, a measure of the cost of insuring against sovereign default, [USN:L5N46C14U TEXT:"jumped to 151.67 basis points"] from Friday's close of 120.21, S&P Global Market Intelligence data showed. As markets tumbled, the Brazilian Treasury cancelled its regular auctions of inflation-linked and fixed-rate government bonds scheduled for October 27 and October 29, respectively. Prices of raw sugar, of which Brazil is a major exporter, slid nearly 5% on the collapsing exchange rate. The plunge is a sharp reversal from the rally seen earlier this month, when markets soared on expectations of a shift to the right when Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, unexpectedly finished first in the opening round of Brazil's presidential elections. The Bovespa index (.BVSP) had closed on Friday almost 7% above its level before the first round, while the real had been nearly 5% stronger against the US dollar. Interest rate futures had also reflected expectations that tighter fiscal policy in the event of a Bolsonaro government would make room for lower borrowing costs. Prediction markets had indicated a Bolsonaro win, with Kalshi pricing in a more than 75% chance of that on Friday. Senator Bolsonaro's refusal to concede and his pledge to seek an annulment added to investor uncertainty. "Important for local financial markets will be how quickly Bolsonaro accepts the result, or at least allows the constitution to run its course," said Chris Turner, strategist at ING in London. Attention will now turn to Lula's choice of finance minister and what it signals about his fiscal approach. "The key signal for markets will be the next Lula administration's commitment to fiscal discipline, starting with the appointment of a new finance minister in coming weeks," said Graham Stock at RBC BlueBay Asset Management. CHALLENGES AHEAD Lula faces the [USN:L1N468127 TEXT:"challenge"] of slowing the rise in Brazil's debt while protecting social programmes and investment, with investors looking for signs his gradual fiscal approach can bring borrowing costs down. "(The) Lula administration will have no choice but to do some fiscal consolidation too, but most investors doubt it will be enough to put debt sustainability back on track," said Thierry Larose, portfolio manager at Vontobel Asset Management. Without confidence that Lula can deliver, lenders could demand higher interest rates, adding to Brazil's debt burden and making credit more expensive for businesses and households. "Investors want a clear and credible commitment to fiscal discipline," said Alejo Czerwonko, chief investment officer for emerging markets at UBS Global Wealth Management. "We expect the rally that followed the first round to be largely priced out, and sentiment to stay weak until a clear fiscal plan emerges," Czerwonko said, adding that investors wanted an end to campaign-related spending and a believable path to stabilize public debt. The reelected president's team aims to produce a budget surplus of about 1.3% of gross domestic product by 2030. "Lula's policies have talked about spending cuts, but he has not gone into the details of how that is going to look," said Divya Singaravelu, head of research at Meridian 1305 Capital.

item.title: Saudi defence pact countries hold talks in Iran as Houthis launch more attacks
item.description: Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday in a bid to de-escalate the Middle East conflict, as Yemen's Houthis launched new attacks on Saudi Arabia and Egypt approved defence support for the Gulf kingdom.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills, Ariba Shahid, Menna Alaaeldin
item.content:encoded: Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday in a bid to de-escalate the Middle East conflict, as Yemen's Houthis [USN:L2N46C045 TEXT:"launched new attacks"] on Saudi Arabia and Egypt [USN:S8N44701K TEXT:"approved defence support"] for the Gulf kingdom. The talks were the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations — which signed the Mecca mutual defence pact in August — since a war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran also spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said the visit was intended to open negotiating channels to "prevent the return of military escalation". Saudi Arabia was represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, younger brother of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir; and Turkey by intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi and Iranian officials said. Iranian state media published pictures of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, attending the meeting. Pakistan and Qatar have led mediation efforts in the war. Qatari mediators [USN:S8N43E021 TEXT:"were in Tehran"] on Sunday, an official told Reuters. Earlier efforts helped produce an [USN:L6N42N0OL TEXT:"interim peace agreement"] in June but fighting between Iran and the United States soon resumed. Conflict then flared between the Iran-aligned Houthis and US ally Saudi Arabia, opening a new front. US AND IRAN THREATEN NEW ATTACKS The wider fighting has restricted shipping through the energy chokepoint of the [USN:L8N3YO10W TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"], pushed up [USN:L2N46B09G TEXT:"global oil and gas prices"], left Gulf states facing missile and drone attacks, and caused a new [USN:L6N4600ML TEXT:"humanitarian crisis"] in Yemen. Tensions between Washington and Tehran have sharpened in recent days. President Donald Trump [USN:L1N469125 TEXT:"said on Friday"] the US may carry out another military operation against Iran. Iranian security officials have told Reuters that Tehran has [USN:L6N46816Q TEXT:"drawn up detailed plans"] to attack Gulf undersea cables if the United States and Israel attack again. The war, which earlier in the year also reignited fighting between Israel and the Iran-backed Lebanese Hezbollah militia, has eroded Trump's approval ratings ahead of the [USN:L6N46017L TEXT:"midterm elections"] that decide control of Congress. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday's discussions would include "Israel’s expansionist policies, developments in the Palestinian territories and Lebanon, and the repercussions of US and Israeli military action against Iran". Baghaei said the meeting, proposed when Munir visited Tehran [USN:L1N4660R4 TEXT:"last week"], could be a first step towards establishing regional security mechanisms. A senior Pakistani security official said the focus of Monday's meeting was to build a regional non-aggression network. The agenda also included US-Iran talks, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the Strait of Hormuz and a US blockade of Iranian ports, the official said. An Iranian official said there would be [USN:S8N42207J TEXT:"no discussion"] of Iran's [USN:L1N45T0JD TEXT:"nuclear programme"] at Monday's meeting and the issue would not be addressed until Tehran's demands for ending the war were met. Those conditions include ending a US blockade of Iranian ports and lifting sanctions on Iranian oil exports. US Vice President JD Vance [USN:L1N45T0DK TEXT:"has said"] Iran must reduce nuclear enrichment to end the war. Pakistan's military media office and Turkey's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. PARLIAMENT APPROVES EGYPTIAN DEFENCE SUPPORT FOR SAUDIS Saudi Arabia has intensified strikes against the Houthis since they captured strategic areas along Yemen's Red Sea coast last month, advancing against Saudi-backed government forces. The Houthis have hit Saudi airports, ports and oil installations. On Monday, the Houthis said they had attacked pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline as well as Riyadh airport, which said it had [USN:L2N46A05D TEXT:"resumed operations"] at two terminals a day earlier. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of the Houthi attacks. The parliament in Egypt, which is not a signatory to the Mecca pact, on Monday authorised the Egyptian military to help defend Saudi Arabia, a major financial and political partner for Cairo. The [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"Mecca Joint Defence Agreement"] says signatories shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised borders, according to a text seen by Reuters. The pact's members held an emergency meeting in Riyadh this month and [USN:L1N45R0S7 TEXT:"agreed to ensure"] the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia. Efforts by Turkey’s parliament to ratify the agreement began last week and are still under way, while Pakistan approved the pact last week.

item.title: Real Madrid defeat Barcelona at Camp Nou to halve gap to LaLiga leaders
item.description: Kylian Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in LaLiga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe. Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended. Real halved the gap to league leaders Barcelona to three points. "It was the most difficult match, against the highest quality opponent, one that had only won in the league," Mourinho told reporters. "For us, it's the victory with the most impressive performance." Both sides created a series of half-chances early on, but Real's forays forward came with far more resolve. Barca manager Hansi Flick's frustration on the touchline served as evidence that Mourinho's [USN:L6N46B0AT TEXT:"game plan"] was functioning better than his own. In the 41st minute, Yan Diomande crossed from the left and Gerard Martin's soft clearance hit the onrushing Mbappe, bouncing off him and into the net. Barcelona had the chance to level before the break after a fortunate ricochet, but Lamine Yamal couldn't convert from close range. It was a set piece that undid Real in the 61st minute, with Pedri's reverse pass finding Raphinha in space in the box and the Brazilian finishing into the corner. Real's swift movement of the ball in their own half continued to expose the Barcelona backline in the early stages of the second half. However, following the goal, the visitors found it increasingly hard to escape Barcelona's pressing. Barcelona's attacks were now finishing with last-ditch blocks from the Real defence, even if Mourinho's side continued to carry a threat going forward. That defensive conviction was rewarded with three minutes remaining. A loose touch from Barcelona substitute Gabriel Jesus set Real on the counter-attack, and substitute Eduardo Camavinga had enough pace to get in behind the defence, before squaring the ball for Mbappe to tap into the empty net. "It's two defeats and we're not happy," Flick told reporters. "We're disappointed. We lacked freshness." The defeat ended Barcelona's nine-match winning start to the league campaign and came days after a 4-2 [USN:L6N4661CR TEXT:"Champions League defeat"] by Paris St Germain. Flick pointed to a demanding run of travel as a factor behind his side's drop in energy levels. "These past few weeks haven't been easy. You only see the matches, but being on a plane for three hours to Seville, returning to the hotel, then going to Paris; it's a lot," he said. "I don't want to talk about this when we lose. It's better when we win, and I won't accept excuses." Barcelona remain top of the standings with 27 points from 10 games, one ahead of Atletico Madrid in second place. Third-place Real Madrid are on 24 points. Earlier Athletic Club beat Getafe 4-0 and Real Sociedad won 2-1 against Levante. Real Betis remain fourth after drawing 0-0 with Celta Vigo.

item.title: Anthropic's path from AI startup to industry-defining IPO
item.description: Anthropic on Monday unveiled its IPO filing, moving closer to what could be the first public listing by a frontier AI lab, outlining the technology's potential while also laying bare the risks and costs of developing it.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic on Monday [USN:L4N45L0EZ TEXT:"unveiled its IPO filing"], moving closer to what could be the first public listing by a frontier AI lab, outlining the technology's potential while also laying bare the risks and costs of developing it. Here is a look at the road to the planned IPO: May 2021: Anthropic, led by siblings Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, announces it has raised $124 million in a Series A funding round led by technology investor and Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn. April 2022: Anthropic raises $580 million in a Series B funding round. March 2023: The company [USN:L1N35L3G1 TEXT:"releases"] a large language model, Claude, that competes directly with offerings from OpenAI. May 2023: Anthropic [USN:L4N37K23L TEXT:"raises $450 million"] from investors including Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and Spark Capital. September 2023: Amazon.com (AMZN.O) [USN:L1N3AY2VF TEXT:"announces"] it will invest up to $4 billion in cash in Anthropic. October 2023: Alphabet's Google [USN:L4N3BX52Q TEXT:"agrees"] to invest up to $2 billion in Anthropic. March 2024: Anthropic [USN:L2N3FH0F3 TEXT:"reveals a suite of AI models"] known as Claude 3. The company says the most capable in the family, Claude 3 Opus, outperforms rival models GPT-4 from OpenAI and Gemini 1.0 Ultra from Google on various benchmarks. August 2024: Anthropic is [USN:L1N3K70J9 TEXT:"hit with a class-action lawsuit"] in California federal court by three authors who say it misused their books and hundreds of thousands of others to train its AI-powered chatbot Claude. November 2024: Amazon.com [USN:L4N3MT10T TEXT:"pumps"] another $4 billion into Anthropic. March 2025: Anthropic [USN:L3N3PF1EX TEXT:"raises $3.5 billion"] at a $61.5 billion post-money valuation led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. September 2025: Anthropic's [USN:L4N3UP19S TEXT:"valuation hits"] $183 billion post-money, after raising $13 billion in a new round. September 2025: Anthropic [USN:L6N3VG0H8 TEXT:"unveils"] the Claude 4.5 AI model, saying the newest version can code for longer uninterrupted stretches and handle finance and scientific tasks better. February 2026: The company [USN:L4N3Z827V TEXT:"raises $30 billion"] in a funding round, more than doubling the Claude chatbot maker's valuation to $380 billion. February 2026: U.S. President Donald Trump [USN:FWN3ZN2FT TEXT:"says"] he is directing the government to stop work with Anthropic, while the Pentagon said it would declare the startup a supply-chain risk. March 2026: Anthropic [USN:L6N3ZR1I4 TEXT:"files a lawsuit"] to block the Pentagon from placing it on a national security blacklist, escalating the AI lab's high-stakes battle with the U.S. military over usage restrictions on its technology. April 2026: Anthropic [USN:L4N40Q0LK TEXT:"debuts Mythos"], its most advanced AI model to date, equipped with sophisticated capabilities and designed for defensive cybersecurity tasks. May 2026: Anthropic announces it has [USN:L4N4251UW TEXT:"raised $65 billion"] at a post-money valuation of $965 billion. June 2026: Anthropic [USN:L4N4291D9 TEXT:"confidentially files"] for a U.S. IPO, edging ahead of rival OpenAI in a closely watched race to reach public markets. July 2026: A federal judge in San Francisco [USN:L6N41W171 TEXT:"signs off"] on Anthropic's landmark $1.5 billion settlement of a class-action lawsuit brought by a group of authors who accused it of misusing their books to train its AI chatbot Claude. August 2026: Independent music publisher Round Hill Music [USN:L6N44E0YF TEXT:"sues Anthropic"] and Suno in California federal court, alleging the AI companies misused hundreds of its songs to train their systems. August 2026: Anthropic is [USN:L6N4480X8 TEXT:"projecting 2028 revenue"] of roughly $190 billion to $200 billion, Reuters reports, citing sources. August 2026: Anthropic's annual revenue run rate [USN:L4N44E1B2 TEXT:"topped $65 billion"] by the end of July, Reuters reports, citing a source. October 2026: Reuters [USN:L6N4611F6 TEXT:"reported"], citing sources, that some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming IPO are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures. October 2026: Anthropic [USN:L1N46404R TEXT:"said"] it is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a public benefit corporation, a legal structure that requires management to balance broader public interests with profitability goals.

item.description: Wall Street ouvre en hausse, optimiste avant une série de résultats et la Fed
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ouvre en hausse, optimiste avant une série de résultats et la Fed 26 octobre (Reuters) - La Bourse de New York a ouvert en hausse lundi, le recul des cours pétroliers contribuant à l'optimisme avant une slave de résultats d'entreprises et la réunion de la Fed. La Bourse brésilienne plonge après la réélection de Lula NEW YORK/BRASÍLIA/LONDRES, 26 octobre (Reuters) - La Bourse de São Paulo a suspendu ses échanges lundi pendant 30 minutes après une chute de 10% de l'indice Bovespa, qui a déclenché un mécanisme de coupe-circuit, au lendemain de la réélection de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva à la présidence du Brésil. Zone euro: Les entreprises rencontrent davantage d'obstacles pour obtenir des crédits, selon une enquête de la BCE FRANCFORT, 26 octobre (Reuters) - Les entreprises de la zone euro ont de plus en plus de mal à obtenir des crédits auprès de leurs banques, tandis que la hausse des prix des carburants et des coûts de production pèse sur leurs finances, montre une enquête publiée lundi par la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). Allemagne: Le climat des affaires s'est amélioré plus que prévu en octobre selon l'institut Ifo 26 octobre (Reuters) - Le moral des entrepreneurs allemands s'est amélioré plus que prévu en octobre, montre une enquête de l'institut Ifo publiée lundi. Eurazeo nomme un Christophe Bavière président du directoire 26 octobre (Reuters) - Christophe Bavière, co-dirigeant d'Eurazeo, a été nommé pour prendre la présidence unique du directoire, a annoncé lundi le groupe d'investissement français, mettant fin à plus de trois ans de double gouvernance. Le patron d’Audi critiqué par IG Metall pour s'être affiché au côté de Trump FRANCFORT, 26 octobre (Reuters) - Le président du directoire d'Audi, filiale de Volkswagen, a été vivement critiqué lundi par la dirigeante d’IG Metall pour sa présence au côté du président américain Donald Trump lors de l’annonce d’un projet d’usine de 4 milliards de dollars (3,57 milliards d'euros) à Perry, en Géorgie. États-Unis: Le moral des ménages se dégrade moins que prévu en octobre, selon une enquête de l'Université du Michigan Le moral des ménages américains s'est dégradé moins que prévu en octobre, montrent vendredi les résultats définitifs de l'enquête mensuelle de l'Université du Michigan. Moody's maintient la note souveraine de la France à "Aa3" L'agence de notation Moody's a décidé vendredi de maintenir la note de crédit de la France à "Aa3", assortie d'une perspective négative, alors que la plupart des analystes s'attendaient à une dégradation à "A1". Stellantis, Bolt et Grand Paris veulent lancer des services de mobilité autonome dès 2028 Stellantis, l'entreprise estonienne de VTC Bolt et la région Île-de-France prévoient de lancer un programme de conduite autonome dans la capitale française en 2028, en utilisant des véhicules du constructeur franco-italo-américain, ont-elles annoncé vendredi dans un communiqué commun. La Royaume-Uni recommande à la population d'avoir des réserves d'urgence pour trois jours Le gouvernement britannique a conseillé vendredi à la population de disposer chez elle de réserves d'urgence pour trois jours, une recommandation qui, selon lui, a été renforcée par le bug logiciel PHP de cette semaine, ainsi que par un été record marqué par la canicule, la sécheresse et les incendies de forêt.

item.description: France: "Plus jamais le 17 octobre", promet Emmanuel Macron
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France: "Plus jamais le 17 octobre", promet Emmanuel Macron PARIS, 26 octobre (Reuters) - Emmanuel Macron a promis lundi de "continuer à tenir" face aux prochaines journées de mobilisation sociale en France et de tout faire pour ne pas réitérer le "traumatisme" du 17 octobre, marqué par des violences, pillages et saccages dans le pays. France: Le gouvernement délivre ses réponses après plus d'un mois de fronde lycéenne PARIS, 26 octobre (Reuters) - Plus d'un mois après le début du mouvement de protestation dans les lycées et les universités en France, qui gagne d'autres pays européens, le gouvernement présente ce lundi une série de mesures pour répondre aux revendications des organisations lycéennes et étudiantes, notamment la refonte de Parcoursup. Suède: La dirigeante du Parti du centre échoue à former un gouvernement et s'en remet au président du Parlement STOCKHOLM, 26 octobre (Reuters) - La dirigeante du Parti du centre suédois, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, n'est pas parvenue à former un nouveau gouvernement et a déclaré lundi qu'il appartenait désormais au président du Parlement, Andreas Norlen, de décider de la suite. France: Laurent Nuñez s'attend à un nouveau samedi "compliqué" le 31 octobre PARIS, 26 octobre (Reuters) - Le gouvernement s'attend à un nouveau samedi "compliqué" le 31 octobre prochain, journée de mobilisation en France à l'appel des "Gilets jaunes" et a prévu un dispositif de sécurité "extrêmement robuste", a déclaré lundi le ministre de l'Intérieur. Marine Le Pen dit vouloir présider à la "Renaissance" de la France ORLEANS, Loiret, 25 octobre (Reuters) - La candidate du Rassemblement National (RN) à l'élection présidentielle de 2027, Marine Le Pen, a dit dimanche vouloir oeuvrer au "redressement" et même à la "renaissance" de la France, en combattant la résignation et le défaitisme qui prévalent selon elle dans le pays. Le suspect de l'attaque dans les Yvelines placé en observation psychiatrique Le suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été placé en observation psychiatrique, le temps d'apprécier si son état de santé est compatible avec la poursuite des auditions, a annoncé dimanche le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT). La garde à vue du suspect de l'attaque de Trappes prolongée La garde à vue du suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et quatre blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été prolongée, a annoncé samedi le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT). Jordan Bardella reconduit à la présidence du Rassemblement national Jordan Bardella a été reconduit samedi à la présidence du Rassemblement national, premier parti d'opposition de France, lors d'un congrès à Orléans (Loiret) où des personnalités de gauche ont participé de leur côté à une manifestation hostile à l'extrême droite. Veillée d'armes avant une nouvelle journée de manifestations, le dispositif sécuritaire renforcé La France se préparait vendredi à une nouvelle journée de manifestations à hauts risques samedi, une semaine après les violences et les pillages survenus en marge de défilés pour les conditions d'enseignement détériorées et contre la vie chère, obligeant l'exécutif à un sursaut. Le Pnat saisi après des tirs dans les Yvelines, sur place Macron dénonce un acte terroriste raciste Le président Emmanuel Macron s'est rendu à Trappes, dans les Yvelines, l'une des communes où un homme à bord d'un véhicule a tiré vendredi à l'arme automatique sur la voie publique, faisant un mort et quatre blessés graves, dont une fille de 12 ans.
